Australia’s domestic spy agency says it has disrupted 16 terrorist threats in the nine months since the Bondi attack, including an antisemi...
articles.body_text:
Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s domestic spy agency says it has disrupted 16 terrorist threats in the nine months since the Bondi attack, including an antisemitic attack, a plot to kill Muslims and a violent racist allegedly found with weapons and ammunition.

The Australian Security and Intelligence Organisation’s director general, Mike Burgess, outlined the “evolving threat” in a speech today on the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terror attacks on the United States.

The Asio chief revealed his organisation had disrupted 16 terror plans since December where the “threat was considered serious but not necessarily imminent”. Burgess previously revealed in June the figure was 14, representing a minor increase. Since 2014, it has foiled 33 major terrorism plots.

Burgess said Sunni violent extremism represented the majority of Asio’s counter-terrorism caseload but that it was “too simplistic to assume there is a single terrorism threat or a most likely terrorist threat as we did in the aftermath of 9/11”.

He said the threats included an individual allegedly inspired by extreme right-wing ideology, others inspired by extreme left-wing ideologies and others inspired by “mixed and seemingly incompatible beliefs”, including one person who allegedly wanted to blow up a school who was allegedly inspired by ideological and extreme Christian beliefs.

double quotation markThese dynamics make the contemporary terrorism environment different – and in some ways, more difficult – than a quarter of a century ago ... Spikes in grievance, intolerance and polarisation are degrading our security environment and making politically motivated violence more likely.

Sarah Hanson-Young on big tech’s ‘attack on democracy’ – Australian Politics podcast

This week, the Albanese government released its draft digital duty of care legislation and announced reforms to allow social media users to opt out of algorithms. The Coalition has ruled out their support, so the Greens will be crucial to the changes passing the Senate.

Political editor Tom McIlroy speaks to the Greens senator Sarah Hanson-Young about why she thinks this will be a “battle for our generation”.

Molly Ticehurst’s killer sentenced to 28 years in jail

Molly Ticehurst’s ex-boyfriend will spend at least 20 years inhas been sentenced to 28 years in jail for her senseless and brutal murder, which was revenge for her reporting allegations of sexual assault to police.

Daniel Billings was sentenced in the Orange Supreme Court today by Justice Natalie Adams, who imposed a non-parole period of 20 years.

Ticehurst, a 28-year-old childcare worker, was found dead in her pyjamas at her home at Forbes, in the state’s central west, in the early hours of 22 April 2024.

Justice Natalie Adams found Billings’ offending was in the high range of seriousness, given he murdered her in the exact way he had long threatened to do.

double quotation markIt must have been absolutely terrifying for Ms Ticehurst to die knowing her worst fears were realised.

Australia’s domestic spy agency says it has disrupted 16 terrorist threats in the nine months since the Bondi attack, including an antisemitic attack, a plot to kill Muslims and a violent racist allegedly found with weapons and ammunition.

The Australian Security and Intelligence Organisation’s director general, Mike Burgess, outlined the “evolving threat” in a speech today on the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terror attacks on the United States.

The Asio chief revealed his organisation had disrupted 16 terror plans since December where the “threat was considered serious but not necessarily imminent”. Burgess previously revealed in June the figure was 14, representing a minor increase. Since 2014, it has foiled 33 major terrorism plots.

Burgess said Sunni violent extremism represented the majority of Asio’s counter-terrorism caseload but that it was “too simplistic to assume there is a single terrorism threat or a most likely terrorist threat as we did in the aftermath of 9/11”.

He said the threats included an individual allegedly inspired by extreme right-wing ideology, others inspired by extreme left-wing ideologies and others inspired by “mixed and seemingly incompatible beliefs”, including one person who allegedly wanted to blow up a school who was allegedly inspired by ideological and extreme Christian beliefs.

double quotation markThese dynamics make the contemporary terrorism environment different – and in some ways, more difficult – than a quarter of a century ago ... Spikes in grievance, intolerance and polarisation are degrading our security environment and making politically motivated violence more likely.

Matt Canavan ‘welcomes’ communication between Barnaby Joyce and Andrew Hastie

Matt Canavan spoke to News24 earlier, saying he “welcomes” Barnaby Joyce reaching out to Andrew Hastie about the One Nation “traitor” cartoon.

Canavan began by condemning One Nation’s bids to “distance” themselves from the cartoon, noting the video was authorised and published by the party.

double quotation markI thought that was pretty weak.

The Nationals leader said he appreciated that Joyce had explained to Hastie that he didn’t know about the cartoon.

double quotation markI welcome Barnaby’s apology, it’s a matter for Andrew if he accepts it – but I think Pauline should do the same.

(In a statement, Hastie said he did accept it, but characterised it as an “explanation” rather than an apology.)

Canavan said he personally welcomed criticism but said that politicians did not need to “devolve” into this sort of language.

The interview took somewhat of an odd turn when Cavanan also referred to himself as someone with “communist sympathies” in his youth.

Albanese is under fire over a grants program that benefited his local golf club. Were any rules broken?

Anthony Albanese is under fire after an invite-only grant program allocated millions to marginal Labor seats and his old local golf club.

The government claims it has broken no rules and delivered its election promises by the standard method but transparency advocates have said the system needs reform and have drawn comparisons to the notorious “sports rorts” affair.

What went wrong – and is this sports rorts all over again?

Marles says Hanson should take Hastie cartoon down and apologise

Back to defence minister Richard Marles, who made some other comments this morning about the One Nation video.

Speaking on Nine, Marles said the Australia’s veteran community would have been affected by the One Nation video’s use of the word “traitor”.

double quotation markOne of the issues here is to use that word in respect of any veteran is taken on by the entire veterans community … it’s distasteful. It’s inappropriate. It should come down and Pauline Hanson should apologise.

The One Nation leader, Pauline Hanson, is standing by the cartoon that labelled Andrew Hastie a “traitor” despite growing condemnation from Labor, the Greens, Liberals and the crossbench.

The video is currently pinned to the top of Hanson’s X feed, and she said on Wednesday she would not apologise and the uproar was “a storm in a teacup as far as I’m concerned”. She has denied ever calling Hastie a traitor.

Last night, Hanson posted a photo of Jacqui Lambie and herself in the Senate, alongside a post that read “I think everyone just needs to take a chill pill”.

A furious Lambie told ABC radio yesterday that Hanson was a “bloody coward”.

The One Nation leader posted again this morning on X to express her “thanks” to Hastie that the “cartoons make the news again”, sharing the “ten best episodes” of the animation Please Explain.

As we reported earlier, Hastie told Guardian Australia he accepted Barnaby Joyce’s explanation that he didn’t know about the cartoon. He said he now knows that Hanson “is the only lying coward”.

Carroll says NFL game in Victoria a moment in the state’s history

The Victoria premier, Ben Carroll, spruiked the NFL game at the MCG this morning, saying it was an exciting and historic day for the state.

double quotation markThe atmosphere, the weather for Melbourne, everything has just come on so perfectly. I couldn’t be more excited to be part of this day.

This event helps cement Victoria as the major events capital, not only of Australia, but of the world.

It’s going to be one of those events that people look back in history and say, ‘Where were you?’ Or ‘I was there’.

Woolworths increased prices of at least four ‘family staples’ during ‘Price Freeze’ promotion

Woolworths raised prices for popular items – including a 33% mark up on chicken fillets – within days of promising to freeze prices on 300 “family staples” for three months to help customers with the cost of living.

Pricing data, compiled by comparison website CW Scanner and provided to Guardian Australia, shows the supermarket chain increasing the prices of at least four key products after starting the three-month “Price Freeze” promotion on 1 May.

The supermarket nearly doubled the price of a 420g can of Woolworths “Mexican Style 3 Bean Mix” during the promotional period – from 60c to $1 on 17 June – the data shows. Woolworths dropped the price back to 60c on 17 August

Woolworths has justified the increases because it regarded the previous prices as promotional prices, rather than the “standard shelf price” for each product.

A Woolworths spokesperson said that the end of a temporary promotion did not represent a shelf price increase.

The NFL is set to hold its first regular-season game in Australia today, a contest between the San Francisco 49ers and the LA Rams.

The showdown will take place at Melbourne’s MCG this morning.

Fans have been turning up in droves. The game starts at 10.35am and you can watch it on Netflix.

articles.title: Trump doubles down on pledge of $5,000 payments if his party retains control of Congress as he address convention a second time – live
articles.excerpt:
President repeats much of his first night’s remarks and leads audience in personalized pledge of allegiance to ‘cheat like hell’ when voting in midterms

Trump promise of $5,000 for US citizens after ...
articles.body_text:
President repeats much of his first night’s remarks and leads audience in personalized pledge of allegiance to ‘cheat like hell’ when voting in midterms

Trump promise of $5,000 for US citizens after midterms decried as ‘bribery’

The president just mentioned the $5,000 for all US adults he has promised if Republicans win the midterm elections. He’s one of the few people to actually mention the pledge on stage tonight.

“We can do that because our country has never done better. We’re taking in trillions, trillions of dollars,” Trump said.

The major legal question of whether this “dividend” actually violates federal law still remains.

Trump’s energy for talking about politics appears to have waned.

“I’ve been doing this now for seven days straight. I want a little music, if you don’t mind,” Trump said, while introducing opera singer Christopher Macchio.

In an improvised pledge of allegiance to himself, Trump directed the audience to commit to voting in the midterm elections at all costs.

The president asked Republicans in the arena to repeat: “I don’t care if I’m registered or not. I’m going to try. And cheat like hell like they do.”

Trump added: “You know what happens if you don’t vote? You go to hell.”

Trump said that voters have to do “the biggest favor you’ve ever done me” and “pretend I’m on the ticket”.

“In a way I am on the ballot,” the president said, despite the fact that many Republicans in battleground states might actually be hampered by yolking themselves to the Trump administration, amid record low approval ratings.

Trump acknowledged that when he’s on the ticket “everybody comes to vote”, but it is still crucial to vote for Republicans in races across the country.

He urged Republicans to turn out and vote for Ken Paxton, the GOP nominee for US Senate in Texas. Once again, Trump took digs at Paxton’s appearance, and even revealed that many advisers pleaded with him to not offer comment.

“I don’t really like the way he looks, I don’t like it,” Trump said. “But you know what I do like? He was the greatest attorney general in the history of Texas.”

The president just mentioned the $5,000 for all US adults he has promised if Republicans win the midterm elections. He’s one of the few people to actually mention the pledge on stage tonight.

“We can do that because our country has never done better. We’re taking in trillions, trillions of dollars,” Trump said.

The major legal question of whether this “dividend” actually violates federal law still remains.

As he runs through what he sees as his main achievements, Trump repeats his false claim that the One Big Beautiful Bill Act has delivered the “largest tax cuts in American history”.

This isn’t true. In fact, these tax cuts aren’t actually in the top five in US history.

Trump praised Vance for his performance on stage, and repeated claims that the venue is “packed” again.

He said he would be “a little bit brief” in his remarks because of his nearly two-hour speech last night.

“I don’t feel like going over the same material again,” the president said.

Donald Trump is, again, walking on stage to a second live performance of God Bless the USA by Lee Greenwood.

As Vance wraps up his remarks, insisting that it’s imperative to send Democrats “packing” in November, the vice-president was another speaker who avoided mentioning Trump’s $5,000 “dividend” to every US adult if Republicans hold on to control of Congress.

Interestingly, Vance doubled down on his criticism of Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for US Senate in Michigan, by chiding him for appearing to suggest that Vance’s grandfather (who helped raised him) wouldn’t approve of the vice-president’s interracial marriage.

“The Democrats are the party of hatred. They’re the party that despises America and the people who built it,” Vance said. “They say that people with names like James Vance are incapable of loving people with names like Usha, and they couldn’t be more wrong.”

Vance continued to urge voters to stay with the Republican party.

“We have done a lot, my friends, and we can do a lot more if we fight together,” he said. “Let’s send these lunatics packing and govern our country for the future.”

JD Vance just used Charlie Kirk as his vehicle to implore voters who may disagree with certain Trump administration policies not to abandon the party in key congressional races this November.

“Charlie hated war. Whether it was Europe or Africa, the Middle East, he didn’t care. He just hated war. That was his view. Now, of course, there are people who love what we’ve done and people who don’t,” Vance said, referring to the ongoing conflict in Iran that has caused prices across the country to spike. “What I’m asking you to do is do what Charlie did: do not throw the baby out with the bathwater. Don’t don’t give the country over to a bunch of crazy people because you happen to disagree with us on a policy issue here or there.”

Vance is now slamming several Democratic nominees in states where Republicans are facing key challenges. This includes James Talarico in Texas and Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan – both of whom are frequent targets of the GOP ahead of November.

“These are the candidates that congressional Democrats have put forth for you to vote for in November,” the vice-president said. “They asked my friends for a one-way ticket to Washington to legislate and regulate and wield power over your lives. Instead, in my opinion, they need a one-way ticket to a mental hospital.”

In many ways this speech is an audition for JD Vance’s possible 2028 presidential run. He’s spent much of his time on stage setting out the threats of the so-called “far left”, the administration’s greatest hits and slamming Joe Biden’s tenure in office.

Vance just acknowledged that a protester interrupted his remarks while waving a Mexican flag.

“Well, my friend, if you love Mexico so much, get your ass over there. I’ll buy you the plane ticket,” Vance said, in a moment that was red meat for the base, and saw chants of “USA” erupt throughout the arena.

Vance, using the birth of his fourth child as a launchpad, addressed “radicals who wish to abolish my family and the thousands and millions of other families all across our country” to “stay the hell away from our kids”.

A quick aside from Vance, who says that his wife – Usha – who gave birth to a son over a month ago, is not in Dallas.

The vice-president recalled that his wife said “hell no” when Republican National Committee (RNC) organizers asked if she would be willing to introduce her husband, just two weeks after giving birth.

“But she sends her love, and I know she’s watching at home,” Vance said.

JD Vance has dedicated a portion of his speech, as we noted earlier, to remember Charlie Kirk – the Turning Point USA founder who was murdered at a campus event in Utah exactly a year ago. Vance and Kirk were close friends.

“Charlie left behind two children, two little kids … I hope that one day they will watch and they will know, and they will understand what I’m trying to say to them tonight. Though they may not appreciate it today, history will record that your father was a great man,” Vance said.

articles.title: Former Carlton president apologises to ex-wife as lewd photo defamation case settles
articles.excerpt:
Luke Sayers says he accepts Cate Sayers did not post photo of his genitals as she says settlement closes ‘painful and difficult chapter’

The embattled former AFL club president Luke Sayers has apolog...
articles.body_text:
Luke Sayers says he accepts Cate Sayers did not post photo of his genitals as she says settlement closes ‘painful and difficult chapter’

The embattled former AFL club president Luke Sayers has apologised to his former wife for the harm he caused as her defamation case over a lewd photo settled.

Lawyers for Sayers, the immediate past president of the Carlton football club, read out the apology in the Victorian supreme court on Friday after indicating the settlement.

“I acknowledge the extreme hurt and harm caused to Cate Sayers by suggesting she posted or may have posted [the lewd photo],” the barrister Sandip Mukerjea said on behalf of Sayers.

“I accept she did not do this. To the extent I may have suggested otherwise, I apologise unreservedly to her.”

Cate Sayers had claimed Luke Sayers had defamed her in a statutory declaration, which accused her of accessing his X account, posting a photograph of his genitals in January 2025 and tagging a female executive at Bupa.

The document was sworn by Luke Sayers in the weeks after the controversial post, which was quickly deleted, as the AFL and Carlton conducted investigations.

In May, Luke Sayers, a former PwC chief executive, applied to have the case transferred to the federal circuit and family court of Australia where the matter would be heard in private.

But Justice Andrew Watson rejected the application in June, finding the supreme court was the more appropriate venue for a defamation claim.

The judge on Friday dismissed the proceedings and commended the parties for reaching the settlement, the terms of which were not discussed in open court.

“All litigation involves time, expense and risk,” Watson said. “There was every reason to expect this proceeding would be no different.”

Outside court, Cate Sayers said she accepted her ex-husband’s apology and the settlement closed a “painful and difficult chapter” for her.

“I commenced these proceedings to establish the truth, clearly and finally,” she told reporters. “With Luke’s apology, I feel I have achieved what I set out to do.”

She thanked the women who had supported her and said she hoped Friday’s outcome gave them the strength to stand up for the truth.

She added that said she wanted to move forward with her life and did not confirm whether the settlement included a monetary component.

Luke Sayers chaired the Carlton board from 2021 to 2025. Before that, he headed consultancy firm PwC Australia between 2012 and 2020.

At an inquiry into a confidentiality and tax scandal in 2023, he apologised while stating he had no knowledge of it during his tenure.

“If the [tax office] had directly and formally advised me as the CEO of PwC Australia ... I would have sought details and ensured a full and thorough investigation,” he said at the time.

articles.title: Megan Rapinoe says women’s sports are facing ‘regression’ of ‘equal rights’ in new Kamala Harris interview
articles.excerpt: Megan Rapinoe is back at it again, defending Angel Reese’s decision to duck the media and "protect her peace." Dan Dakich isn't buying it. Since when is skipping out on the job "taking power back"? Da...
articles.body_text:
Megan Rapinoe is back at it again, defending Angel Reese’s decision to duck the media and "protect her peace." Dan Dakich isn't buying it. Since when is skipping out on the job "taking power back"? Dan breaks down why the modern sports culture of "all empowerment, no accountability" is a disease that’s actually hurting the growth of women’s sports.

You thought Kamala Harris was done after getting summarily beaten in the 2024 presidential election by Donald Trump? Think again.

The former vice president is right back at it, laughing it up with friends, discussing her future in politics, and avoiding any and all difficult questions she does not have prepared answers to.

On Thursday, Harris joined former US women’s soccer player and political activist Megan Rapinoe for a fawning new interview on "Why Are You Like This?" where she touched on important questions, like, "Why are you so amazing?"

SMUG MEGAN RAPINOE GOES ON UNHINGED RANT, ATTACKS RILEY GAINES AND SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM OVER WOMEN'S SPORTS

Former US women's national team player Megan Rapinoe gave her take on the US men's team's World Cup loss to Belgium. (Photo by Soobum Im/USSF/Getty Images))

"You could do anything, you’re brilliant, and you’re talented, and you’re beautiful, and you’re smart, and you’re funny and you’re all these things," Rapinoe said in an incredible moment of journalism. The context for this question is Rapinoe's wondering why Harris chose to go into politics because she would be reminded that she’s "still a woman" and "still black."

Her answer? Well, not much. Determination, enjoying hard work, and some barrier breaking, of course. As for her upbringing, Harris said that she was taken to "marches" in a "stroller" by her parents, which she associates with her educational and political choices later on.

While the interview is light on important topics around women’s sports, Rapinoe couldn’t help herself when talking about her own experiences and what we’ve supposedly lost since her playing career ended.

Former Vice President Kamala Harris speaks at the State of the People POWER Tour opening ceremony on June 6, 2025 in Los Angeles, Calif. (Mario Tama/Getty Images)

"I’m thinking about my own experience being a female athlete, and I went through, in the prime of my career, just the most historic time in women’s sports," she said. "I mean, it was crazy in the best ways. We saw a huge amount of progress, which has led into a pretty significant regression in terms of just equal rights and people’s rights in general. I definitely think those two are tied."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

What rights have women in sports lost? Is she implying that because there are now limitations on males in women's sports, women are losing their rights?

The reality is precisely the reverse. Had a male athlete occupied Rapinoe's spot on the US women's soccer team, she would never have achieved the level of success and the accomplishments that defined her career.

Not to mention that male athletes are not prevented from playing sports, they're simply required to play sports against other males. That's the only reasonable and rational position, which is why Rapinoe opposes it so fiercely.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Rapinoe then tries to tie women's sports being "different" to men's sports to governing "as a woman," to which Harris laughs aggressively, then responds with, "Well, I've always been a woman, so I don't know what to tell you," which about sums up the level of scintillating intellectual discussion present throughout the episode.

Harris then goes on a fascinatingly inept tangent, saying that in order to describe her experience as a woman in politics, she wants Rapinoe to close her eyes and picture someone based on four words: "the boy next door."

"Now you have a sense of what he looks like," Harris continues. He probably plays softball, he probably lives somewhere in suburban America. He's a good kid."

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

Do boys play softball? What is she talking about?

Former Vice President Kamala Harris speaks during the 10th Austrian World Summit climate conference at the Hofburg Palace in Vienna, Austria, on June 16, 2026. (Anadolu via Getty Images)

Harris brings the comparison home by saying, "What four words together in our language would describe you or me?," then adds, "we don't have it."

Well, there are plenty of four-word phrases to describe Megan Rapinoe and Kamala Harris actually, just none that they would like.

Later in the interview, Harris says that "We have increasingly witnessed a concentration of wealth and power among a few, to the exclusion of the most, and that wealth and concentration being also a political power."

Obviously, Harris is excluded from this, despite being an extremely wealthy woman who just purchased an $8 million house in Malibu with a heated pool and in-ground spa. Joe Biden is excluded from this, despite his decades-long career in politics and his son, Hunter, using his influence with the former vice president and eventual president to increase his wealth. Barack Obama is excluded from this, despite owning multiple mansions, including a beautiful Martha's Vineyard estate.

As for whether the very wealthy Harris will run again for the 2028 nomination? She hasn't decided, she told Rapinoe. God help us all if she does.

The interview as a whole illustrates a central reason Harris fell short in 2024: her campaign and her party were, and continue to be, represented by figures such as Rapinoe. Who believe that males should play in women's sports and that every day is an opportunity for grievance. Harris has no meaningful insights to make about herself, politics, or how to improve the country. Only vague hand waving about the need to change things.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

There's been no "regression" in women's rights in recent years, and if anything, the rise in popularity for sports like the WNBA has made it more obvious how important it is to protect those athletes. Both physically and in terms of competitive fairness. Rapinoe can't accept that, because it undermines her and Harris' worldview. Reality often does.

articles.title: Molly Ticehurst’s killer Daniel Billings sentenced to 28 years in jail for her murder
articles.excerpt:
Ticehurst’s former partner had pleaded guilty to stabbing her 15 times at her Forbes home just before midnight on 21 April 2024

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breakin...
articles.body_text:
Ticehurst’s former partner had pleaded guilty to stabbing her 15 times at her Forbes home just before midnight on 21 April 2024

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Molly Ticehurst’s ex-boyfriend has been sentenced to 28 years in jail for her senseless and brutal murder, which was revenge for her reporting allegations of sexual assault to police.

Daniel Billings was sentenced in the NSW supreme court in Orange today by Justice Natalie Adams, who imposed a non-parole period of 20 years.

Billings stood calm and expressionless when the sentence was handed down on Friday morning.

Ticehurst, a 28-year-old childcare worker, was found dead in her pyjamas at her home at Forbes, in the state’s central west, in the early hours of 22 April 2024.

Billings, her former boyfriend, broke into her bedroom and used a hunting knife to stab her 15 times in a ferocious attack that lasted less than a minute.

Adams found Billings’ offending was in the high range of seriousness, given he murdered her in the exact way he had long threatened to do.

“It must have been absolutely terrifying for Ms Ticehurst to die knowing her worst fears were realised,” Adams said.

The 31-year-old former mine worker had repeatedly threatened to smash into Ticehurst’s bedroom and kill her in the months after she ended their on-and-off relationship in December 2023, according to police documents.

Ticehurst reported this abuse to the police, who charged him with several counts of sexual assault and a series of domestic violence stalking and intimidation charges.

He was also charged with killing Ticehurst’s dachshund puppy with a hammer after an earlier break-up.

Police took out a provisional apprehended violence order against Billings, barring him from entering Forbes.

Billings, who previously lived in Dalby, Queensland, spent one night in police custody but was freed on bail by a local court registrar a fortnight before the murder as there was no judge on duty that weekend.

Upon his conditional release, Billings became enraged and obsessed with a belief he had been wrongfully accused of rape.

He viewed himself as a victim of injustice, also angered by his claim that police threw his Queensland State of Origin boxing team singlet in the dirt.

In a series of videos Billings recorded on his phone in the hours before the murder, he detailed his plans of harming Ticehurst in revenge.

“Molly Jean Ticehurst, well, you’ve done it, you’ve succeeded in whatever you wanted out of all of this, whether I get to you tonight or not,” Billings said in one of the recordings, made on the afternoon of 21 April.

Adams sentenced Billings to a maximum term of 28 years for what she described as a brutal attack. She found Billings acted out of retribution, revenge and “extreme hatred” for Ticehurst, angry after she reported the rape allegations.

The murder was also a serious public justice offence, as Billings killed the only witness in his potential rape trial, the judge said.

Adams offered her condolences to the Ticehurst family. “It is clear that Molly’s senseless death has had a significant impact on those who loved her,” she said.

Gaby Shepherd held up a large image of her slain friend when Billings entered the courtroom and sat in the dock.

Billings did not look in her direction, instead staring straight ahead and shaking his head any time the sexual assault allegations were mentioned by the judge.

Prosecutors did not seek a life sentence for Billings.

Billings pleaded guilty to murder after more than 500 days of legal negotiations, which led to the sexual assault charges being dropped in November 2025.

Charges of property damage, the animal cruelty offence and breaching the apprehended violence order were taken into consideration in the sentence.

Ticehurst’s murder intensified a national campaign against domestic and gendered violence. The movement sparked changes to NSW laws, including stripping registrars of the power to grant bail, “show cause” thresholds for domestic violence-related bail applications and electronic monitoring for accused people.

Billings will be eligible for parole in April 2044.

articles.title: Charlie Kirk supporters return to site of assassination 1 year later: ‘We are still standing’
articles.excerpt:
Sage Lloyd says students who witnessed Kirk’s assassination refused to walk away or be silenced as a new statue was unveiled.

One year after Charlie Kirk was assassinated at Utah Valley University, t...
articles.body_text:
Sage Lloyd says students who witnessed Kirk’s assassination refused to walk away or be silenced as a new statue was unveiled.

One year after Charlie Kirk was assassinated at Utah Valley University, the people who stood feet from him when he was killed returned to the campus Thursday night in what Turning Point USA (TPUSA) described as a deliberate effort to "reclaim" the space in his honor.

"We’re doing an event in Utah right now at UVU, a deliberate act reclaiming that space in his honor and for his legacy," TPUSA spokesman and "The Charlie Kirk Show" Executive Producer Andrew Kolvet told Fox News host Jesse Watters Thursday night.

Andrew Sypher, TPUSA’s chief field officer, told the gathering at UVU in Orem that he had been standing about 10 feet to Kirk’s left when the fatal shot rang out on Sept. 10, 2025.

CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION: NEW UVU PRESIDENT SAYS IT WILL CONTINUE TO ‘HOST THE FRAYS,’ EMBRACE FREE SPEECH

A view of the location where Charlie Kirk was shot one year ago. (Alec Thornock for Fox News Digital)

"Steps from these doors is the ground where evil unfolded," Sypher said. "We did not come back to rehearse the crime scene."

Instead, Sypher said, they returned because "this is where they tried to end him" and "this is where we refuse to let the last word be a gunshot."

ERIKA KIRK URGES CONSERVATIVE STUDENTS NOT TO BACK DOWN IN FIRST SCHOOL YEAR SINCE CHARLIE'S ASSASSINATION

For the students of UVU’s TPUSA chapter, the anniversary marked a return to the campus where some witnessed Kirk’s assassination.

"A year ago, our lives changed forever," chapter President Sage Lloyd told the crowd.

Lloyd said students experienced "fear, grief, confusion, and heartbreak" and had every reason to walk away.

INSIDE CHARLIE KIRK’S EFFORT TO DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF CONSERVATIVE VOICES

People gather around a large wooden cross on a grass lawn in a campus courtyard at Utah Valley University in Orem, Utah, Thursday. Turning Point USA hosted its "Freedom Built to Last" memorial service to mark the first anniversary of founder Charlie Kirk's death at the courtyard site. (Getty Images)

"We could have packed our bags. We could have stepped away," she said.

Despite the tragedy, the TPUSA chapter stayed.

"The same students who witnessed a political assassination are willing to stand up, speak out and keep moving forward," Lloyd said.

"We can let it define us through fear, or we can let it strengthen us through courage," she added. "The Turning Point chapter at UVU has made our decision, and we chose courage."

Sypher also revealed what he said was a text Kirk sent him on the morning he was assassinated.

SURVEILLANCE VIDEO TIMELINE TRACKS ACCUSED CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSIN ACROSS UVU CAMPUS BEFORE FATAL ROOFTOP SHOT

Floral tributes and a prayer vigil sign are placed next to large concrete planters at Utah Valley University in Orem, Utah, Thursday, at the exact campus location where Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk was fatally shot one year ago. (Getty Images)

"Andrew, I’m not here to pick a fight. I am here to show them kindness," Kirk wrote, according to Sypher.

"That was the assignment this time," Sypher said. "To talk with students who hate you. To share the truth, and to not become cruel doing it."

"Charlie’s assassination did not put our faith to death," Sypher told the crowd. "It woke it up."

The service was marked with worship performances and video tributes to the fallen conservative leader, as well as an unveiling of a new statue to stay on campus at UVU.

ERIKA KIRK PENS ESSAY ON GRIEF AS READERS GAIN INSIGHTS INTO WRENCHING PAST YEAR

Kirk’s widow, Erika Kirk, separately marked the anniversary with a black-and-white photograph from their wedding showing the couple holding hands.

Across the image were two words: "...until Heaven."

The university closed its campus for the one-year anniversary. UVU itself did not organize the memorial, but university President Dr. Jon Anderson previously told Fox News Digital the school supported TPUSA using campus space for its event.

Lloyd closed her remarks with a message about what returning to UVU meant for Kirk’s student movement.

"Our chapter is still here, we are still speaking, and we are nowhere near done," she said. "And that is how his voice lives on."

Fox News Digital's Michael Ruiz contributed to this reporting.

Jasmine Baehr is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital, where she covers politics, the military, legal debates surrounding life and family policy, as well as faith and culture.

Vice President JD Vance blasted a heckler waving foreign flags and yelling at him from the GOP convention floor during his primetime keynote address Thursday night.

"What the people at home missed is that we just had a protester interrupting us and waving the Mexican flag.," he said. "Well, my friend, if you love Mexico so much, get your a– over there. I'll buy you the plane ticket."

JD VANCE TO INVOKE CHARLIE KIRK, FAMILY ‘BIRTHRIGHT’ IN FIERY MIDTERM KEYNOTE SPEECH THRASHING DEMS

A protestor throws a Mexican flag as US Vice President JD Vance speaks during the second day of the Republican National Committee midterm convention at the American Airlines Center in Dallas, Texas on September 10, 2026. US Republicans are betting that putting President Donald Trump at the center of their campaign can rescue a party facing grim election forecasts, despite the president's negative approval ratings. A day earlier, on the first day of the midterm convention, he promised $5,000 to every American adult if Republicans retain control of Congress in November. (Brendan SMIALOWSKI / AFP via Getty Images)

The crowd erupted into chants of "USA! USA! USA!" as the troublemaker was escorted out of the event.

articles.title: Brazil’s Supreme Court shuts down early as political chaos mounts
articles.excerpt:
Brazil’s Supreme Court has cancelled a second straight day of deliberations as suspicions of corruption, political bias and police interference loom over several of its members.

Cancellations are rar...
articles.body_text:
Brazil’s Supreme Court has cancelled a second straight day of deliberations as suspicions of corruption, political bias and police interference loom over several of its members.

Cancellations are rare at the high court. But on Thursday, Chief Justice Luiz Edson Fachin nixed a second consecutive session, calling for the court to reconvene on Tuesday instead.

The decision was spurred by an ongoing crisis among the court’s members.

The divisions emerged on September 1, when one justice, Andre Mendonca, unsealed a series of federal police documents that appeared to show a disgraced banker, Daniel Vorcaro, seeking advice from another justice, Alexandre de Moraes.

De Moraes has rocketed to prominence in recent years for his roles in high-profile cases.

He presided over the trial of former President Jair Bolsonaro after prosecutors accused the far-right leader of plotting a coup following his 2022 election defeat. De Moraes also oversaw suspensions of platforms like X and Rumble for failing to abide by court orders, making him a target for Brazil’s right wing.

The document release authorised by Mendonca, a Bolsonaro appointee, contains roughly 30 text messages sent to a phone number associated with de Moraes, allegedly from Vorcaro.

In response, de Moraes has accused Mendonca of abusing his authority on the court for political gains. He requested a probe into whether Mendonca interviewed Vorcaro without the presence of police or prosecutors.

Tuesday’s session will involve the full Supreme Court bench, and 10 of the justices will discuss whether the 11th member, de Moraes, should be investigated over the text messages.

The tit-for-tat on Brazil’s high court is the latest fallout from the Banco Master corruption scandal.

Vorcaro, the head of the Banco Master financial institution, was arrested in November 2025 on accusations he defrauded investors of billions in lost funds, in one of the biggest banking scandals in the country’s history.

The collapse of Banco Master’s private banking arm left behind more than $7bn in debt.

Lawmakers from across the political spectrum have become embroiled in the unfolding scandal as new details emerge.

The turmoil risks affecting October’s general elections, including a pivotal presidential election.

Left-wing incumbent Lula Inacio Lula da Silva is set to compete for the presidency against Jair Bolsonaro’s eldest son, Senator Flavio Bolsonaro.

Both Lula and Senator Bolsonaro have called for investigations into the Supreme Court justices.

The Bolsonaro family itself has been dragged into the Banco Master scandal. In May, the publication Intercept Brasil released a report showing that Senator Bolsonaro petitioned Vorcaro for funds to finance a film about his ex-president father, who is now serving a 27-year prison sentence.

Senator Bolsonaro has denied wrongdoing, claiming he did nothing more than seek private sponsorship for the film, entitled Dark Horse.

But on Thursday, Brazilian police executed dozens of raids related to the Banco Master scandal, including some that targeted two figures involved in the film: Karina Gama, the head of a production company, and Congressman Mario Frias, who served as executive producer.

Senator Bolsonaro has called the probes “attempted political interference” ahead of the elections.

articles.title: Clippers face federal criminal probe after NBA punishes team over Kawhi Leonard deals
articles.excerpt: Dan breaks down Mina Kimes’ comments, Charlotte Wilder’s defense of women in sports, the difference between journalism and commentary, and why he believes Taylor McGregor represents the type of report...
articles.body_text:
Dan breaks down Mina Kimes’ comments, Charlotte Wilder’s defense of women in sports, the difference between journalism and commentary, and why he believes Taylor McGregor represents the type of reporting that deserves recognition.

Federal prosecutors have launched a criminal investigation into allegations that the Los Angeles Clippers arranged secret, off-the-books sponsorship deals for Kawhi Leonard to circumvent the NBA’s salary cap, first reported by The New York Times.

The inquiry is being handled by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of New York in Brooklyn, which has previously pursued major sports integrity cases involving NBA referee gambling and FIFA corruption.

Los Angeles Clippers forward Kawhi Leonard, right, looks toward the scoreboard during the second half of an NBA basketball game in Inglewood, California, on May 1, 2025. (AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill, file)

Federal authorities began scrutinizing the Clippers’ alleged conduct before the NBA announced its penalties, including a $30 million fine, the forfeiture of five consecutive first-round picks from 2029 through 2033 and a one-year suspension for owner Steve Ballmer. Two top Clippers executives also received suspensions.

MALIK BEASLEY INDICTED ON FEDERAL CHARGES FOR ALLEGEDLY FIXING HIS OWN NBA PERFORMANCES FOR BETTORS

The Times reported that a grand jury has already issued at least one subpoena in the investigation.

Investigators are zeroing in on undisclosed endorsement deals, including a reported $28 million agreement with Aspiration Partners.

The green finance company later collapsed into bankruptcy, while co-founder Joe Sanberg was sentenced to 14 years in federal prison for fraud.

Connie Ballmer, wife of former Microsoft CEO and Los Angeles Clippers owner Steve Ballmer, made a whopping $80 million contribution to NPR last month. (Rodin Eckenroth/FilmMagic)

Prosecutors are examining whether Clippers owner Steve Ballmer and team executives helped facilitate side deals that compensated Leonard beyond the NBA’s salary-cap limits.

The SEC has also entered the investigation. Daktronics, which supplied displays for the Clippers’ Intuit Dome, confirmed that regulators requested records tied to its sponsorship agreements with Leonard.

The federal investigation significantly escalates the Clippers’ scandal, which the NBA called a "pattern of misconduct" after a yearlong review by the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Leonard’s uncle and manager, Dennis Robertson, received a five-year ban from the NBA, while Leonard was ordered to pay $700,000 in restitution.

The Clippers strongly rejected the NBA’s findings, accusing the league of conducting a biased investigation designed to justify a predetermined narrative.

A detailed view of the Los Angeles Clippers logo at center court before the game against the Oklahoma City Thunder at Intuit Dome on March 23, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Luke Hales/Getty Images)

"We vehemently reject the NBA’s findings, which are the result of a heavily biased investigation seeking to justify a predetermined narrative rather than facts and evidence," the franchise said in a statement.

The team added, "We intend to vigorously challenge these findings and penalties through every avenue available to us and look forward to an ethical and impartial arbitration process."

David Kelley, Ballmer’s attorney, called the NBA’s investigation a "witch hunt" and a "gross injustice" in a letter to Commissioner Adam Silver.

DODGERS OWNER MARK WALTER DENIES REPORTS, SAYS TEAM PAYROLL IS SUPPORTED BY REVENUE: 'THERE HAS BEEN NO FRAUD'

Kelley argued that league officials privately acknowledged facts that contradicted the NBA’s public position.

"League counsel has acknowledged in our discussions that the league does not believe there was an agreement between the Clippers and Aspiration to funnel money to Kawhi Leonard," Kelley wrote.

He also emphasized that federal authorities previously determined Ballmer was "a victim of Joe Sanberg’s fraud, not a participant."

Leonard defended his conduct while acknowledging mistakes by members of his inner circle.

"Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am," Leonard said. "I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family."

Leonard added that he entered into his Clippers contract and the other agreements "in good faith," with no knowledge of any effort to circumvent the salary cap.

LA Clippers forward Kawhi Leonard (2) controls the ball in the first quarter against the Denver Nuggets during game seven of the first round of the 2025 NBA Playoffs at Ball Arena in Denver, Colorado, on May 3, 2025. (Ron Chenoy/Imagn Images)

Ballmer and the Clippers are considering a federal lawsuit against the NBA to block the sanctions.

The criminal investigation could complicate that effort. Civil litigation may be delayed if key witnesses invoke their Fifth Amendment rights against self-incrimination.

Spokespersons for the U.S. Attorney’s Office, the Clippers and the NBA declined to comment on the investigation.

Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

Alejandro Avila is a longtime writer at OutKick, living in Southern California.

articles.title: Texas reports first equine infection of New World screwworm on ranch horse
articles.excerpt:
The flesh-eating parasite had been largely eradicated,  but now authorities are racing to contain an outbreak

A horse in southern Texas has been infected with the New World screwworm, marking the fir...
articles.body_text:
The flesh-eating parasite had been largely eradicated,  but now authorities are racing to contain an outbreak

A horse in southern Texas has been infected with the New World screwworm, marking the first US equine infection as health authorities race to contain an outbreak of the flesh-eating parasite.

The pest was discovered on the hind limb of a working ranch horse in Presidio county, according to a statement on Thursday from US Equestrian Foundation.

The foundation advised horse owners to monitor the animals daily for wounds, foul odor or maggots.

The screwworm, a fly larva, can nestle into and infest open wounds.

“Check horses daily, keep wounds clean and covered as directed by your veterinarian, use veterinarian-recommended fly control products and limit fly access with physical barriers such as fly masks, sheets and clean stabling practices when appropriate,” the foundation’s statement read.

The Texas Animal Health Commission, has restricted the movement of warm-blooded animals outside of infested zones in parts of Presidio and Jeff Davis counties, among several others, to curb new infestations.

After being eradicated decades ago, the screwworm was detected in June on a calf in Zavala county, near the US-Mexico border. A screwworm infestation has spread throughout Mexico.

Of the 49 US cases recorded this year, all have been in Texas, except for one in New Mexico, where the pest was found on a dog, according to the US Department of Agriculture.

The resurgence of the parasite, which can cause severe injury or death in animals, has raised alarm about potential financial devastation to Texas ranchers.

Greg Abbott, the Texas governor, issued a disaster proclamation in June to mobilize state resources toward coping with the rising screwworm presence.

Before the pest was reported on American soil, the Trump administration announced the launch of a sterile fly dispersal facility in Edinburg. If female screwworm flies mate with a sterile fly, their offspring will not be viable, thus curbing the population.

articles.title: Juror on Lindsay Clancy trial says 'we let down Lindsay' following mistrial
articles.excerpt: Fox News national correspondent Bryan Llenas sits down with defense attorney Kevin Reddington to discuss the mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy case and Reddington’s motion seeking a not guilty finding by...
articles.body_text:
Fox News national correspondent Bryan Llenas sits down with defense attorney Kevin Reddington to discuss the mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy case and Reddington’s motion seeking a not guilty finding by reason of insanity.

A juror on the high-profile Lindsay Clancy murder trial in Massachusetts said she believes the jury "let down Lindsay" and that it was "hard to separate the children from what our task was."

Clancy was on trial for strangling and killing her three young children in January 2023 after sending her then-husband, Patrick, out to pick up medication and takeout. When he returned, he found Clancy injured outside after an apparent suicide attempt and the children unconscious in the basement. Two children died that night, while the third was airlifted to a Boston hospital and died several days later.

The trial ended in a mistrial last week after the jury failed to reach a unanimous verdict. Eleven jurors sided with finding Clancy not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility — Massachusetts’ version of an insanity defense — while one holdout favored finding her criminally responsible.

"Everybody says you're not supposed to feel like you failed, but you have a task to come out unanimous. And we tried everything we could to get to that end. And I feel like we let down Lindsay," Paula, 65, who was one of the jurors who sided with the majority, told WCVB.

LINDSAY CLANCY LAWYER SAYS HE PLANS NEW MOTION TO DISMISS AFTER JURORS SPEAK OUT ON MISTRIAL: REPORT

A juror on the high-profile Lindsay Clancy trial in Massachusetts said she believes the jury "let down Lindsay." (Greg Derr/Pool The Patriot Ledger via AP)

Clancy's legal team did not dispute that she killed her children but argued that she should not be found criminally responsible because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis. Clancy also admitted in court filings to killing her three children, but claimed that severe mental illness left her not criminally responsible.

Paula said the jury's majority believed that Clancy needed help and that the healthcare system failed her, adding that she thinks the medical community should do more to support women with postpartum mental health issues.

"There was a clear indication that the medical community failed her and not just her, but her whole family, because something like that affects the whole entire family. And if everybody can be educated in a better way, then it will help the whole family unit," Paula said.

After attorneys made their arguments, Paula said the jurors were sent to deliberate with 297 pieces of evidence, including Patrick's emotional 911 call, which she said some jurors had trouble listening to during deliberations.

"We all tried to help each other. It was hard to separate the children from what our task was, and it was very emotional," she said.

The jurors polled themselves at the start of deliberations, at which point eight believed Clancy was not guilty due to lack of criminal responsibility, two thought she was guilty and two were undecided, Paula said.

The majority eventually came to the belief that Clancy was not guilty due to lack of criminal responsibility.

Lindsay Clancy's legal team did not dispute that she killed her children but argued that she should not be found criminally responsible because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis. (Boston Globe via Getty Images)

Prosecutors argued during trial that Clancy was criminally responsible for the killings despite evidence that she suffered from mental illness.

"We did not start out 11 to one," Paula said. "Everybody had different opinions and different reasons and different ways that they got there."

Paula said the majority had a hard time understanding why the one holdout wanted to vote to convict Clancy.

"We did not feel that he was following the law because he admitted that he had doubt at different times, that he had doubt about the case that was presented, and the way that the rule read to all the rest of us is if we had doubt, then we could not convict her of first-degree murder or second-degree murder or manslaughter," Paula said.

The foreperson then sent a note to the judge saying the jury could not reach a verdict and accusing the holdout of refusing to apply the law on reasonable doubt.

Judge William Sullivan called up each of the jurors and individually asked them if they could apply the law as he had explained it, and they reportedly answered in the affirmative.

"The judge has to believe that people are telling him the truth. And so, you know, 11 people told the truth and one maybe didn't. And I will never know why," Paula said.

Paula said she believed it would have been worth restarting deliberations with an alternate if the court had removed the holdout.

Lindsay Clancy was on trial for strangling and killing her three young children in January 2023 after sending her then-husband, Patrick, out to pick up medication and takeout. (Pool)

ACCUSED NC KILLER MOM PLANS INSANITY DEFENSE — AS RETIRED JUDGE SAYS MORE MAY FOLLOW LINDSAY CLANCY STRATEGY

"If our holdout juror had given us evidence to support his reasoning, we would have felt differently about what we told the judge," Paula said.

Other jurors have also spoken out in recent days to take issue with the holdout's position.

"He had the hardest time getting off the fact that Lindsay viciously killed her children," juror Kellie Farina previously told NBC10 Boston.

On Thursday, Clancy's defense filed a motion arguing the prosecution failed to meet its burden and asked the judge to enter a required finding of not guilty, which the defense argues would prevent a retrial.

articles.title: Top GOP senator reveals what Dem colleagues are fretting about behind closed doors
articles.excerpt:
Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso, R-Wyo., revealed to Fox News Digital that his Democratic colleagues quietly worry about their party's "far, far left" future.

DALLAS — As Republicans huddle for a ...
articles.body_text:
Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso, R-Wyo., revealed to Fox News Digital that his Democratic colleagues quietly worry about their party's "far, far left" future.

DALLAS — As Republicans huddle for a last show of unity before the home stretch of the midterm elections, a top Senate Republican revealed what his Democratic colleagues are predicting about the future of their party.

Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso, R-Wyo., told Fox News Digital that in private, his colleagues across the aisle are wringing their hands over the insurgent progressive wave that has fast become the standard-bearer of the Democratic Party during this election cycle.

"It's surprising how the energy of the Democrat Party has moved to the far, far left," Barrasso said during an interview at the Republican National Committee midterm convention.

TOP REPUBLICAN NAMES WHO HE SAYS IS REALLY LEADING DEMOCRATS — AND IT'S NOT SCHUMER OR JEFFRIES

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., departs after a weekly Senate Democratic Policy luncheon at the US Capitol in Washington, DC on July 29, 2026. (Alex Wroblewski / AFP via Getty Images)

"Those are the people that are driving the party. And the concern that I have, talking to other colleagues in the Senate, who they’ll say that is the future of their party," he continued.

Republicans are trying to fight against history and anxious voters feeling the crunch on their wallets, and as the war in Iran continues to sputter on without a clear end in sight.

The convention in Dallas is meant to hammer home that while President Donald Trump’s name isn’t on the ballot, his agenda, and the incumbents and fresh candidates that could execute it, are.

TRUMP'S $5,000 DIVIDEND CHECKS WOULD COME WITH A MAJOR CATCH UNDER GOP SENATOR'S PLAN

While that push to energize Trump’s base to hit the polls in November ensues, key races across the Senate map have seen progressive and far-left candidates emerge as the standard-bearers for the party during this cycle.

Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, James Talarico in Texas and Peggy Flanagan in Minnesota all bucked expectations, and the Democratic old guard in Washington, D.C., including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., to earned the nomination in their respective races.

REPUBLICAN SOUNDS ALARM ON RISING DEM STAR: 'THIS GUY’S GOING TO BE A PROBLEM'

Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso, R-Wyo., speaks to reporters after voting at the U.S. Capitol on March 4, 2026. Senate Republicans rejected a Democratic-backed war powers resolution aimed at limiting President Donald Trump's military campaign against Iran. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

El-Sayed and Talarico, in particular, have been targeted heavily during the convention, which Trump declared was, in part, dedicated to ensuring Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton would win out and prevent the Lone Star State from turning a shade of purple.

"And we cannot allow that to become the future of our country," Barrasso said. "So that's, to me, the reason that we need to win all of these races, why it's so critical, is that these people that are winning the Democrat primaries, I believe, would be terrible for our nation."

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

articles.title: Patrol sergeant accused of murdering sheriff’s captain in yearslong romantic dispute over woman they dated
articles.excerpt:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A North Carolina highway patrol sergeant has been indicted in the murder of a sheriff’s captain following a years-long...
articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A North Carolina highway patrol sergeant has been indicted in the murder of a sheriff’s captain following a years-long romantic dispute involving a woman both officers dated, according to authorities.

North Carolina State Highway Patrol Sgt. Nekime Matu Oxendine, 44, reportedly shot Cumberland County Sheriff’s Capt. Adam Bean on March 27 outside the woman’s home in Hope Mills following a confrontation between the two men, according to authorities.

Police arrived to find the woman, Tara Lynn Whitman, performing CPR on Bean as Oxendine remained nearby, according to search warrant filings. Bean was pronounced dead at the scene, officials said.

The fatal shooting followed years of escalating tension surrounding Whitman’s relationships with both men, state investigators wrote in court filings.

FORMER COLLEAGUES DETAIL CHP CAPTAIN’S SPIRAL BEFORE ALLEGED MURDER-FOR-HIRE PLOT AGAINST HUSBAND

Cumberland County Sheriff’s Capt. Adam Bean was fatally shot on March 27 following a domestic confrontation. (Cumberland County Sheriff's Office)

According to investigators, Oxendine had displayed persistent jealousy and insecurity over the years regarding Whitman’s connection to Bean.

According to the warrant, Whitman began dating Bean in 2022 after ending a long-term relationship with Oxendine. She eventually ended that relationship and returned to Oxendine.

FLORIDA DEPUTY KILLED EX-GIRLFRIEND OVER A TV, THEN HIMSELF, SHERIFF SAYS

While Whitman was with Bean, Oxendine appeared to exhibit increasingly concerning behavior, according to text messages cited in the warrant. Whitman and Bean had described some of his behavior as "stalking," documents reported.

"I seen u have been talking to Adam!!! Best wishes!!!" Oxendine wrote in one message.

"Better tell that Mother F—er to get ready too!!! " he added.

Oxendine also sent messages questioning Whitman’s decision to stay with Bean, demanding to know the truth and claiming he knew where Bean lived, according to the warrant.

In December 2025, Whitman eventually resumed her romantic relationship with Oxendine, moving out of the home she shared with Bean.

FILE — The Cumberland County Jail building is pictured in North Carolina. Cumberland County Sheriff’s Capt. Adam Bean was fatally shot following a romantic dispute, authorities said. (Derek Davis/Portland Press Herald via Getty Images)

For the next three months, however, Oxendine continued to show insecurity over Bean, asking Whitman whether Bean was more attractive and accusing him of having the power to "lure u in and out of my life on demand." He also sought continued reassurance about Whitman’s commitment, according to the warrant

Then, on the night of March 27, Bean asked Whitman to come to his residence after work to talk. Whitman initially agreed but later stopped responding to his messages.

When Whitman did not show up, Bean messaged her, "F— it, I’ll come to you," and threatened to blow his car horn and cause a scene if she did not come outside.

When Bean arrived, he became irate after seeing Oxendine’s vehicle parked outside, according to the warrant.

Oxendine stepped outside and fired about two warning shots into the ground. Bean continued advancing toward him, and Oxendine then opened fire two to three more times, according to the warrant.

Bean collapsed onto his back in the yard, according to the warrant. Police said they found a handgun and magazine nearby.

Oxendine has been charged with first-degree murder.

FILE — A North Carolina State Highway Patrol vehicle drives through high water. Sgt. Nekime Matu Oxendine, a state highway patrol sergeant, was indicted in Bean’s killing. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

Bean had served with the Cumberland County Sheriff’s Office for 20 years and most recently served as assistant chief of detectives with the rank of captain.

He was posthumously recognized with the Merit Award for his outstanding service, forward-thinking leadership, initiative and lasting contributions to the Cumberland County Sheriff’s Office.

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

articles.title: Trump tells Dallas crowd the Luka Dončić trade 'might go down as the worst in sports history'
articles.excerpt: Fox News senior White House correspondent Peter Doocy questions President Donald Trump about one of the biggest debates in basketball history—Michael Jordan versus LeBron James—following James' blockb...
articles.body_text:
Fox News senior White House correspondent Peter Doocy questions President Donald Trump about one of the biggest debates in basketball history—Michael Jordan versus LeBron James—following James' blockbuster decision to join the Philadelphia 76ers. During the exchange, Doocy asks the president to weigh in on which NBA legend he believes deserves the title of the greatest player of all time, as fans continue to debate Jordan's six championship legacy against LeBron's longevity, all-around dominance, and latest career move to Philadelphia.

President Donald Trump used his appearance in Dallas to dunk all over the Mavericks’ infamous trade of Luka Dončić.

Speaking at the Republican National Committee’s midterm convention on Wednesday night, Trump stood in American Airlines Center, the old home of Dončić before being traded to the Los Angeles Lakers, where he added a major jab to the Mavericks midway through his remarks.

"I must tell you, I don’t understand the trade," he said. "That trade is not good."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

President Donald Trump speaks during the Republican convention at American Airlines Center on Sept. 9, 2026, in Dallas, Texas. (Chitose Suzuki/The Dallas Morning News via Getty Images)

Dončić, Maxi Kleber, and Markieff Morris were traded to the Lakers in exchange for Anthony Davis, Max Christie and a 2029 first-round draft pick in February 2025.

It was a deal that sent a shockwave through the entire NBA. In fact, sports fans in general were baffled that Dončić would be teaming up with LeBron James out west, while the Mavericks traded away their franchise cornerstone.

After all, Dončić carried the Mavericks to the 2024 NBA Finals just the season prior.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

So, Trump didn’t mince words about how he felt this trade would go down in history.

"It’s not going to go down as the greatest trade in the history of sports," he said. "It might go down as the worst trade in the history of sports."

Trump did say, though, that Babe Ruth being traded from the Boston Red Sox to the New York Yankees remains the worst trade in sports history. But he thinks the Mavericks will get to the point where they regret dealing Dončić away.

President Donald Trump arrives to speak during the first day of the Republican Midterm Convention at the American Airlines Center in Dallas, Texas, on Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026. (Bloomberg)

"Maybe we can redo that trade?" Trump said. "I redo deals all the time."

The Dallas crowd gave Trump a loud cheer when he mentioned it, which is hardly surprising considering how unhappy Mavs fans were when GM Nico Harrison dealt Dončić. Some fans even held a "funeral" for Dončić outside American Airlines Center, mourning the loss of their franchise star.

Dončić never requested a trade from the Mavericks, which made it even more surprising. Also, the Mavericks exclusively spoke with the Lakers about the trade instead of getting the best offer from across the league.

Harrison strongly defended the decision at the time, arguing that "defense wins championships" when justifying the move to trade Dončić for a rim protector in Davis. However, Harrison’s mindset didn’t show up on the court, and he was eventually ousted from his post in the front office.

Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) controls the ball against the Atlanta Hawks during the first half at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, Ga., on Nov. 8, 2025. (Dale Zanine/Imagn Images)

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

The trade definitely looks better for the Lakers, though James is now playing for the Philadelphia 76ers entering the 2026-27 season. Dončić is averaging 31.9 points, 8.1 assists and 7.8 rebounds since joining Los Angeles.

Scott Thompson is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Restaurant chain once frequented by Kardashians files for bankruptcy after 36 years
articles.excerpt: Marmalade Cafe, a Southern California restaurant fixture founded in 1990, has filed for Chapter 11 protection amid rent disputes, supplier obligations and broader losses affecting the dining industry....
articles.body_text:
Marmalade Cafe, a Southern California restaurant fixture founded in 1990, has filed for Chapter 11 protection amid rent disputes, supplier obligations and broader losses affecting the dining industry.

Another longtime American restaurant chain is fighting to keep its doors open as mounting debt and financial losses batter the dining industry.

Marmalade Cafe, a 36-year-old Southern California brunch favorite, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection Sept. 2, citing "rent disputes and mounting supplier debts."

It owes more than $1 million to Gilmore Farmers Market, US Foods, Sysco Ventura Inc., the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration and others, according to multiple reports.

The Encino-based company listed total assets of $12.7 million in the filing but reported a net loss of $680,314, according to the New York Post.

LONGEST-RUNNING RED LOBSTER LOCATION IN AMERICA IS CLOSING AFTER 56 YEARS

Over the years, the chain, which first opened in Santa Monica in 1990, evolved from a grab-and-go spot to offering private dining and catering to businesses, including Boeing, Mattel, CBS and Warner Bros. Studios. The Calabasas location was even a favorite of the Kardashians, according to reports.

The Calabasas Marmalade Cafe closed after nearly 30 years as construction disrupted parking and drove down sales. (PG/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images)

It was operating just four locations across Southern California at the time of the filing after closing four others in recent years. The company cited hardships, including "unsustainable financial losses and a lack of rent relief," according to the filing.

BEFORE MCDONALD'S AND STARBUCKS, AMERICANS PACKED THESE ONCE-BELOVED LUNCH COUNTERS

The Calabasas restaurant closed after construction disrupted parking and drove down sales; its Santa Monica location shuttered amid losses tied to the Palisades Fire; and the Original Farmers Market outpost closed after failing to regain pre-pandemic business, the Los Angeles Times reported.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"Unfortunately, the ongoing construction throughout the shopping center has resulted in a devastating decline in business," the restaurant wrote in a Facebook post in July about the Calabasas closure.

The Marmalade Cafe in Calabasas was frequented by the Kardashians. (PG/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images)

"Despite our best efforts to weather these challenges, and after seeking rent relief from our landlord during this extended construction period, the landlord declined to help," the statement continued. "With construction expected to continue for an extended period, we simply cannot sustain the financial losses any longer."

That closure was reportedly a main catalyst for the bankruptcy filing.

Marmalade Cafe's four remaining locations in El Segundo, Malibu, Sherman Oaks and Westlake Village remain open, and a representative told the Los Angeles Times they are "very healthy and very strong."

Longtime restaurants are being squeezed by simultaneous increases in rent, wages, insurance and utilities, chef Andrew Gruel, founder of American Gravy and a Huntington Beach city councilman, told Fox News Digital.

While many chains go bankrupt, chef Andrew Gruel predicts the restaurants that will survive are those that can adapt their overall business models to industry shifts. (iStock)

"Marmalade's Chapter 11 filing is a prime example of how difficult the restaurant business has become, particularly in California," Gruel said.

"Longevity and a loyal customer base are valuable, but they don't necessarily protect a restaurant when the underlying cost structure changes faster than the business can adapt."

The filing also stated that the company had downsized from more than 200 employees to about 50 as of this year.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Marmalade Cafe is the latest in a string of restaurant bankruptcies and closures across the Golden State and nationwide.

Other recent casualties include Fireman Hospitality; Salad and Go; FAT Brands, the parent company of Fatburger; Johnny Rockets and other chains. Red Lobster, Carl's Jr. and On the Border locations have also recently shuttered.

Marmalade Cafe joins a growing list of restaurant chains facing financial trouble, including On the Border. (Alex Martin/Greenville News/USA Today Network via Imagn Images)

The closures do not necessarily mean the restaurants were poorly run, Gruel added. Rather, rising costs can catch up with even established businesses, part of an industry reset he expects will bring more closures.

"The operators who survive will likely be those who can adapt their menus, staffing, hours, footprint and overall business model while maintaining the experience that brings customers back," he said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Marmalade Cafe for comment.

Deirdre Bardolf is a lifestyle writer with Fox News Digital.

articles.title: A.J. Brown suffers apparent injury in Patriots debut against Seattle Seahawks in Week 1
articles.excerpt: The New England Patriots open up the 2026/27 NFL season in a Super Bowl LX rematch with the Seattle Seahawks. Nick Wright, Chris Broussard, and Kevin Wildes ask if Drake Maye can have a statement game...
articles.body_text:
The New England Patriots open up the 2026/27 NFL season in a Super Bowl LX rematch with the Seattle Seahawks. Nick Wright, Chris Broussard, and Kevin Wildes ask if Drake Maye can have a statement game, what another good season would mean for Sam Darnold being elite, and if Brock Purdy and the San Francisco 49ers can outplay Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams.

A.J. Brown’s highly anticipated debut with the New England Patriots was interrupted by an apparent injury in the third quarter of Wednesday’s NFL season opener.

Brown appeared to suffer the injury while trying to make a catch at Lumen Field against the Seattle Seahawks. The game was billed as a rematch of Super Bowl LX, which Seattle won in February by defeating New England 29-10 to claim the franchise’s second Vince Lombardi Trophy.

New England led 10-0 when Brown exited the game Wednesday.

INJURY BUG BITES 49ERS AGAIN AS TEAM LOSES KEY DEFENSIVE TACKLE DURING PRACTICE IN AUSTRALIA

New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown (1) reacts after suffering an apparent injury during the third quarter of a game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on Sept. 9, 2026, in Seattle, Wash. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images)

Brown went down after a Seahawks defender rolled into him and remained on the field after the play. After medical personnel tended to Brown on the field, he made his way to the sideline without assistance. He later entered the blue medical tent before eventually heading to the locker room wearing only one cleat.

New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown (1) reacts after suffering an apparent injury during the third quarter of a game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on Sept. 9, 2026, in Seattle, Wash. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images)

Brown was later ruled out for the remainder of the game because of what was described as an ankle injury. Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold left the game in the first quarter and was later ruled out. Drew Lock replaced Darnold under center for Seattle.

New England took a 10-3 lead over Seattle into the fourth quarter.

Chantz Martin is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Fetterman teases where his true loyalty lies after surprise appearance at GOP convention
articles.excerpt:
Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., calls himself a "commonsense Democrat," rejects socialism and praises Republican Sen. Dave McCormick in a video appearance at the RNC Midterm Convention in Dallas.

DALLAS ...
articles.body_text:
Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., calls himself a "commonsense Democrat," rejects socialism and praises Republican Sen. Dave McCormick in a video appearance at the RNC Midterm Convention in Dallas.

DALLAS — A rogue Senate Democrat toying with the idea of leaving his party drew a hard line in the sand after making a surprise appearance at the GOP’s Trump-centric convention.

Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., has been welcomed with open arms by Republicans to join the party after he floated leaving his own caucus, and spurred further speculation that he would jump ship after dropping a video introducing his colleague, Sen. Dave McCormick, R-Pa., at the Republican National Committee’s midterm convention on Wednesday.

But in a statement to Fox News Digital, the progressive-turned centrist said that he wasn’t turning his back on the Democratic Party, even as the knives have come out to cut him loose from the Senate.

DEM SENATOR DELIVERS SURPRISE VIDEO AT REPUBLICAN CONVENTION BACKING MCCORMICK

Senator John Fetterman, D-Pa., left, pictured alongside Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., right (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images; Heather Diehl/Getty Images)

"My remarks introduced Dave McCormick as a great American and friend. We are in different parties, but we are both Team PA," Fetterman said. "We have delivered hundreds of millions of dollars back to Pennsylvania, fought for improved transportation and affordable housing, and the Steel Way of Life."

"I’m a lifelong Democrat who votes overwhelmingly with my party — and should the Senate flip in November, I will still be the 51st vote that I ran on," he continued.

Fetterman started his career in the Senate after besting Dr. Mehmet Oz in a tight race for power in 2022, where he clinched a historically thin Democratic majority in 2022 running on a progressive platform.

TOP REPUBLICAN NAMES WHO HE SAYS IS REALLY LEADING DEMOCRATS — AND IT'S NOT SCHUMER OR JEFFRIES

But since then, he has become a thorn in Democrats’ side, and challenged the direction of the party.

Earlier this year, Fetterman warned that if Democrats became more entrenched in anti-Israel policy positions, he would exit the party, and has taken jabs at the party’s direction during this midterm election cycle as far-left progressives, like Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, have emerged as standard-bearers.

Fetterman has routinely bucked Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and his colleagues on a handful of key issues, like President Donald Trump’s war in Iran or voting with Republicans to end the marathon government shutdown last Fall.

FETTERMAN FACES DEM REVOLT AS BOMBSHELL REPORT FUELS PUSH TO OUST HIM: 'DISGRACE'

Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., speaks during a Senate Republicans press conference at the U.S. Capitol on June 2, 2026, flanked by Sen. James Lankford, R-Okla., and Sen. Shelley Moore Capito, R-W.Va. (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc)

His latest edict followed a bombshell report that alleged through leaked texts with his aides that the maverick Democrat would often brush off duties of his office, like meeting with paralyzed veterans or charging that a three-hour funeral service for slain police officers was a "non-starter."

And Republicans would gladly welcome him into the fold. Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said in July that he and others in the Senate GOP have had "had conversations with him in the past … about the challenges he faces in his caucus."
