articles.title: DAVID MARCUS: Congress set to protect AM radio and American discourse
articles.excerpt:
FCC Chairman Brendan Carr joined ‘Pod Force One’ to discuss the Trump administration’s push to ‘rebalance’ the media by encouraging local broadcasters to air more pro-America programming.

In 2026, th...
articles.body_text:
FCC Chairman Brendan Carr joined ‘Pod Force One’ to discuss the Trump administration’s push to ‘rebalance’ the media by encouraging local broadcasters to air more pro-America programming.

In 2026, the WFMD radio station in Frederick, Maryland, is celebrating its 90th year on the AM airwaves, and thanks to a bipartisan bill set for a vote in Congress this week, every new car sold in America will have an AM antenna to pick up its signal.

The AM Radio For Every Vehicle Act already has more than 300 co-sponsors in the House, 60 in the Senate, and has been pitched mainly as a measure to ensure that emergency messages — the ones that start with the shrill whistle — can be sent out to cars through the AM stations.

The common sense measure is a good plan B to have in place in cases of cyberattacks or cyber outages, because sometimes the old ways can be the best ways.

FILE — If the bill passes, every new car sold in America will have an AM antenna to pick up its signal. (Rolf Vennenbernd/picture alliance via Getty Images)

STEVE FORBES, STEPHEN MOORE: AMERICA MUST FREE ITS AIRWAVES BEFORE CHINA PULLS AHEAD

That is a laudable goal, and by itself enough to warrant the legislation. But in fact, this measure can do more than protect lives, it can protect civil American discourse. AM radio is one of the last vestiges of it we have left in this digital age.

All across the country, there are little stations like WFMD, with a predictable schedule that starts with a light-hearted but local-news-heavy morning show, then late-morning to mid-afternoon nationally syndicated news shows, followed by an afternoon drive-time call-in show that covers local, state and federal politics.

In Frederick, the local afternoon show "Mid-Maryland Live" belongs to Tim May and Frank Mitchell: the former, a cantankerous conservative wordsmith with a Maryland twang, and the latter, the patient and pleasant liberal New York City transplant with the dulcet radio voice.

FILE - Some argue national topics are heard first on local radio stations. (Joe Amon/The Denver Post via Getty Images)

FCC CHAIR SUGGESTS ABC SKIPPING TRUMP'S SPEECH WILL FACTOR IN LICENSE RENEWAL DECISION

The discourse that Tim and Frank engage in for three hours a day, along with the callers — many of whom are long-time regulars — is arguably the most balanced view of what is happening in the world that one could ask for, and almost always free from yelling and vitriol.

Local AM radio is also the most reliable way to know what matters to people in communities outside major cities. For example, while data centers are a relatively new issue in the macro news ecosystem, I have been hearing about it for well over a year on local AM stations all over the country.

It was almost never inchoate rage or unvarnished praise over data centers, but rather a very nuanced conversation from listeners who understand the laws and regulations of their communities with almost encyclopedic knowledge.

We live at a time when, perhaps rightfully, we bemoan the demise of so many local small town newspapers along with the coverage and accountability they used to provide. But in many ways, that slack has been picked up by AM radio, where appearances by local officials are extremely common.

ABC HAS NO BUSINESS ON PUBLIC AIRWAVES BECAUSE IT OPERATES 'LIKE A PARTISAN CABLE NETWORK,’ WATCHDOG TELLS FCC

These same stations are usually also the repository for high school sports, giving kids the chance to feel that their effort matters when their exploits are broadcast live to the community.

Some small government types might object to the government handing local AM radio stations this boon of enforcing access to their product, but it is a much more sensible way to help the radio industry than the National Public Radio model of direct funding.

We have all seen that, for a myriad of reasons, publicly funded radio — absent the constraints of the free market — always winds up extremely far left. But local AM radio keeps the lights on by selling ads, usually to local businesses, and has a financial incentive to create a broad, cross-aisle appeal.

FILE - Estimates suggest that 80-90% of Americans listen to AM or FM radio each week. (Sjöberg Bildbyrå/ullstein bild via Getty Images)

For those who think radio is a dying form, think again. Estimates suggest that 80-90% of Americans listen to AM or FM radio weekly, with more than 80% of car owners flipping it on when they fire up the engine.

No, AM radio is not heading to the dustbin of history. Not now, and not anytime soon. Just as our parents and grandparents did, we tune in to get the weather or the traffic, or just to find out what is going on. Not in New York, not in D.C., but where we live.

The fact that our Congress, which would struggle to pass "Go" in Monopoly, is set to pass the AM Radio For Every Vehicle Act is a testament to the enduring power of our local radio stations, and a good sign that listeners in Frederick will have Tim and Frank to listen to for a long, long time.

David Marcus is a columnist living in West Virginia and the author of "Charade: The COVID Lies That Crushed A Nation."

articles.excerpt: Michele Tafoya believes FIFA made the RIGHT call reversing Flo Balogun's red card, BLASTS Alicia Keys, and speaks against the WNBA leadership following Congress's letter to Cathy Engelbert demanding a...
articles.body_text:
Michele Tafoya believes FIFA made the RIGHT call reversing Flo Balogun's red card, BLASTS Alicia Keys, and speaks against the WNBA leadership following Congress's letter to Cathy Engelbert demanding answers for Caitlin Clark.

Team USA got all it could handle from Italy in Sunday's FIBA Women's World Cup game.

The Stars and Stripes jumped out to a 19-8 lead by the end of the first quarter and held on to win by a score of 55-52, though the contest wasn't without its fair share of lead changes and controversies.

Italy led by three midway through the fourth quarter and even had a chance to tie the game on the final shot where an Italian player looked like she may have been fouled.

CAITLIN CLARK NOT IN TEAM USA'S STARTING 5 FOR FIBA WOMEN'S BASKETBALL WORLD CUP OPENER VS CHINA

Caitlin Clark #12 of the USA Basketball Women's National Team looks on during a game against the Italy Women's National Team during the 2026 FIBA World Cup Qualifying Tournament on Sept. 6 at Berlin Arena in Berlin, Germany. (NBAE via Getty Images)

But the game-tying attempt sailed to the left of the rim and landed harmlessly into the arms of Breanna Stewart, ending the threat.

Team USA shot a putrid 1-12 from beyond the arc (8%) and only made 29% of their field goals overall, highlighting just how much work still needs to be done if this team wants to make a run at the title.

ANGEL REESE VS. 7'3" DOUGHY CHINESE TOWER ZHANG ZIYU WAS A BATTLE FOR THE AGES AT THE FIBA WORLD CUP

Italy's Cecilia Zandalasini led all scorers with 14 points to go along with seven rebounds and was the unquestioned star in a game full of them.

Napheesa Collier, Kahleah Copper, Breanna Stewart and Chelsea Gray of the USA Women's National Team look on during a game against China at the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup 2026 on Sept. 4, 2026, at Max-Schmeling-Halle in Berlin, Germany. (NBAE)

For the Americans, Jackie Young led with a team-high 10 points and was the only player to shoot above 40% from the field.

CAITLIN CLARK AND ANGEL REESE MUST NOW WORK TOGETHER AT WOMEN'S WORLD CUP AS WNBA TAKES A HIGH-STAKES BREAK

Had the Italians hung on to win, it would have been one of the most monumental upsets in FIBA Women's World Cup history.

With the win, the U.S. women improved to 2-0 in group play and have now qualified for the quarterfinals of the tournament.

Caitlin Clark during the Women's FIBA World Cup 2026 between the U.S. and China on Sept. 4, 2026, in Berlin, Germany. (NurPhoto)

Time will tell if this group of women has what it takes to bring some hardware home from Germany, but if they don't want to leave empty-handed, they will need their heavy hitters to step up, namely Caitlin Clark, who finished with just one point and was held without a field goal for the entire game.

articles.title: News live: parents of Australian surfers killed in Mexico fly in for trial; Labor pressured to toughen lobbying rules
articles.excerpt:
The parents of Australian brothers Callum and Jake Robinson, who were killed in Mexico in 2024, will fly to Ensenada to attend the aggravated homicide trial of their accused killers.

The two surfers,...
articles.body_text:
The parents of Australian brothers Callum and Jake Robinson, who were killed in Mexico in 2024, will fly to Ensenada to attend the aggravated homicide trial of their accused killers.

The two surfers, aged 33 and 30, and their friend, Jack Carter Rhoad, 30, a US citizen, had been camping in a remote beachside area when they were killed in what investigators believe was an attempt to steal their vehicle.

Writing on Facebook, Debra and Martin Robinson said attending the trial felt “overwhelmingly difficult” but that “being in that courtroom is one of the last things we can do for Callum and Jake”.

double quotation markWe are going because we need to be there, not only for ourselves, but to represent the immense love, heartbreak and unimaginable loss felt by their families, friends and everyone who loved these three extraordinary young men.

We want to hear the truth. We want to understand what happened. And most importantly, we want to be their voices, because they can no longer speak for themselves.

In 2025, a Mexican court sentenced a woman to 20 years in prison for her involvement in the incident.

Scale of illegal cigarette market changes dynamics of pricing, Butler says

Butler is asked about the ongoing barney over tobacco – the opposition and One Nation are proposing big drops in excise rates to make legal cigarettes more affordable. He says the price of cigarettes is a proven disincentive to smoking but that the scale of the illegal market has “changed the dynamics of that”:

double quotation markThere’s there’s no question we have a very serious challenge on our hands as a country with the scale of the illegal market.

Every country has illegal cigarettes. The scale of the illegal market here has exploded over the last three or four years, and that’s a huge law enforcement challenge for us.

‘Unremarkable’ to make big tech responsible: Butler

The health minister, Mark Butler, is up on ABC Radio National (RN). He dismisses the opposition’s claims that the government’s digital duty of care legislation amounts to censorship:

double quotation markIt’s pretty unremarkable, really, to expect that big companies have a duty of care not to harm Australian citizens, particularly, frankly, young Australians.

He likens it to the introduction of seatbelts in the 1970s, which people at the time saw as an infringement on civil liberties.

Further details on what constitutes harmful content will be announced this week, he says. Asked whether there’s a threat social media companies could withdraw their platforms, he says:

double quotation markWell, they always make that threat, don’t they.

One Nation propose divert super payments to pay packet

One Nation has come up with a plan to give people their superannuation earlier, reducing the amount they’ll have at retirement in exchange for a current cash boost.

Pauline Hanson says under their plan anyone paying rent or a mortgage can take up to a quarter of their super as a “pay boost” for up to three years.

It would keep the same tax rate as it would have in super, she says, saying someone on $90,500 would get $44 a week.

Hanson has been targeting super for a while. The government points out that people can access their money for financial hardship or compassionate reasons, while experts say that super forces people to save and gives us a sustainable retirement system:

Anniversary of death of last known Tasmanian tiger

It’s National Threatened Species Day today. Many papers have run full-page ads from a range of conservation organisations noting that it is the anniversary of the death of the last Tasmanian tiger – the last known one, that is.

The environment minister, Murray Watt, says the government has protected 274 species and 16 ecological communities threatened with extinction and is dealing with multiple threats, including climate change, invasive species and diseases including bird flu. He said:

double quotation markWe remain committed to long-term environmental recovery, in partnership with state and local governments, conservation groups, wildlife experts and local communities.

We are making good progress towards our target of protecting 30% of Australia’s land, to preserve vital habitat for our precious species.

Independent to launch bill to regulate automated decision-making algorithms and tools

The independent member for Curtin, Kate Chaney, will put forward a bill to establish Australia’s first legislated mandatory framework for the use of automated decision-making in government this week.

The use of the controversial tool within the aged care sector has affected hundreds of applications for out-of-home care.

Almost a fifth of older Australians who contested their algorithm-determined Support at Home funding allocation had a higher level of support or higher priority allocated once a human reviewed the decision.

Chaney said there was no transparency in government about how widely used automated decision-making tools are. She told ABC Radio National:

double quotation markIt’s not clear if there’s a human who can actually apply a common-sense overlay to these decisions. And it’s not clear how you can review these if they’re made by a computer.

So the bill that I’m introducing today would actually create a mandatory framework that applies whenever government is using an automated system to make a decision that affects people’s significant rights and would require those three things to be addressed: transparency, human oversight, and review.

Good morning, all – Tory Shepherd here for today’s blog.

Parliament is, of course, sitting. Much of the focus will be on the government’s crackdown on social media.

They’re planning to beef up the eSafety commissioner’s powers and to release draft legislation for a digital duty of care, which will force big tech to stop harmful content and to allow users to opt out of algorithms.

There’ll be more to come, but you can read Tom McIlroy’s piece here.

In an opinion piece, the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, argues the existing ban on social media for under-16s is working (not everyone is convinced of that), and says they will strengthen it.

He says the digital duty of care legislation will “put the onus on services providers to take reasonable steps to create a safe online environment for all Australians” and give people control over algorithms:

double quotation markThey are driving users – often young people – down rabbit holes of harmful content.

We also know harmful algorithms can be devastating for young people and body-image issues.

For young men, those paths far too often lead to misogynistic voices detached from the values and expectations of our societies.

The communications minister, Anika Wells, has challenged the Coalition and the Greens to pass legislation strengthening powers for the eSafety Commissioner related to the social media ban for under 16s.

Labor will try to secure passage of the legislation in parliament this week. It would toughen information-gathering powers to investigate non-compliance by social media platforms related to the ban, and double the maximum penalty for breaches to nearly $110m.

A Senate committee recommended the bill be passed in August. Wells said:

double quotation markIt’s been more than two months since the Albanese government introduced an urgent law to strengthen eSafety’s powers to enforce the social media minimum age law.

Australian kids and parents needed these laws eight weeks ago, but the Coalition and Greens teamed up to send our four-page bill to an eight-week inquiry.

double quotation markThis is the kind of dawdling and delay that has enabled social media companies to get away with harming our kids for so long.

Two more Australians will join humanitarian and rescue efforts in the devastating Nepal-Tibet floods.

Two social workers have joined a total of 49 Australian personnel assisting in the disaster.

Monday has been declared a National Day of Mourning in Nepal, with the death toll reaching nearly 1,400.

Some 36 Australians are among the nearly 5,000 people who remain unaccounted for.

A cross-party group of dad MPs in federal parliament will champion new data showing the importance of fathers spending quality time with their kids, as they push for new progress on parental leave.

A new “Dads Caucus” will launch on Monday in Canberra, including Labor’s special envoy for men’s health, Dan Repacholi, the assistant minister for immigration, Matt Thistlethwaite, and MPs including Josh Burns, Jerome Laxale, Peter Khalil and the Liberal shadow minister Aaron Violi.

Supported by Movember, the launch event will include appearances by Wiggle Lachlan Gillespie, Jebediah frontman Kevin Mitchell, Joel Phillips (the film-maker father of the Eastern Rosellas song’s young composer) and author and Movember ambassador Zach Perez.

Movember’s More Time With Dad Report shows 70% of fathers who take parental leave said it was good for their mental health, 83% said it helped them bond with their child, and 78% said it was beneficial for their relationship with their partner.

But currently almost a third of fathers take no parental leave at all, and of those who did take leave, a majority (56%) said it wasn’t enough.

Movember wants to work with the Albanese government to establish a cross-departmental working group and to lead a review of the next phase of paid parental leave rules in Australia.

A coalition of 75 charities, social service organisations and transparency campaigners have called on the federal government to introduce a national lobbying act, to better control efforts to influence decision-makers in Canberra.

Representing millions of members, the groups span advocates for the environment, human rights, regional communities, faith organisations and online campaigners. Together, they argue the federal lobbying register and controls from the attorney-general’s department and Parliament House are badly insufficient for the public interest.

Australian Democracy Network’s chief executive, Saffron Zomer, said the breadth of support showed that lobbying reform was no longer a specialist integrity issue.

“Organisations working on very different issues share the same experience: well-resourced interests have greater access to government, while much of that influence remains hidden from public view,” she said.

“If the same professional lobbying activity is taking place, the same rules should apply. We have a crisis of public trust in government, and we can’t rebuild this trust without transparency.”

The parents of Australian brothers Callum and Jake Robinson, who were killed in Mexico in 2024, will fly to Ensenada to attend the aggravated homicide trial of their accused killers.

The two surfers, aged 33 and 30, and their friend, Jack Carter Rhoad, 30, a US citizen, had been camping in a remote beachside area when they were killed in what investigators believe was an attempt to steal their vehicle.

Writing on Facebook, Debra and Martin Robinson said attending the trial felt “overwhelmingly difficult” but that “being in that courtroom is one of the last things we can do for Callum and Jake”.

double quotation markWe are going because we need to be there, not only for ourselves, but to represent the immense love, heartbreak and unimaginable loss felt by their families, friends and everyone who loved these three extraordinary young men.

We want to hear the truth. We want to understand what happened. And most importantly, we want to be their voices, because they can no longer speak for themselves.

In 2025, a Mexican court sentenced a woman to 20 years in prison for her involvement in the incident.

Welcome to Monday’s live coverage. Tory Shepherd will be with you shortly for the day’s news.

articles.title: Has National Championship picture in college football already changed after a stunning first week?
articles.excerpt:
Joel Klatt breaks down the biggest storylines of 2026 CFB season.

Week one of the 2026 college football season isn't fully in the books, and already the playoff and National Championship picture has ...
articles.body_text:
Joel Klatt breaks down the biggest storylines of 2026 CFB season.

Week one of the 2026 college football season isn't fully in the books, and already the playoff and National Championship picture has already been turned upside down. And the balance of power within the two top conferences might have shifted, unexpectedly, after some shocking performances, both good and bad.

While the Indiana Hoosiers are defending national champions, finished off a 16-0 season, and brought in another impressive transfer portal class under Curt Cignetti, most have expected that the Big Ten Championship will run through two other programs: the Ohio State Buckeyes and Oregon Ducks.

Ohio State lived up to the billing, with an overwhelmingly dominant win over Ball State. Far from a top opponent, sure, but the Buckeyes did exactly what they needed to as the country's number one team in their opening game. Oregon though? Not exactly.

OREGON RALLIES FROM SLOW START, THWARTS BOISE STATE'S UPSET BID IN SEASON OPENER

Oregon’s Davon Benjamin and Brandon Finney Jr. celebrate after a play during a college football game against Boise State at Autzen Stadium on Sept. 5, 2026, in Eugene, Oregon. (Al Sermeno/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

The Ducks struggled for most of the first half against Boise State, then found themselves tied with just over eight minutes to go in the game after a Broncos field goal. But after a quick touchdown drive to take a 34-27 lead, the Oregon defense stiffened, and closed out the win with back-to-back stops. That said, the Ducks dominated more than the scoreline indicated. They averaged nearly eight yards per play, allowing just 4.2 to Boise State. They had 10 yards per attempt passing, with 28 completions on 38 attempts for 378 yards, while adding three sacks and four tackles for loss on defense. The scoreline was close, but Ducks fans can be encouraged that they "deserved" a more decisive outcome.

Then there's the "second tier" of the Big Ten, teams that have hoped coaching staff changes and another year of development for start quarterbacks will make the difference: Michigan and USC. SC brought in defensive coordinator Gary Patterson to finally make the Trojans defensive unit championship quality. Michigan, after a year of turmoil after the firing of Sherrone Moore, hired Kyle Whittingham away from Utah, a head coach known for his consistency and steadiness.

Their outcomes on Saturday couldn't have been more different.

ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 05: Dom Nichols #8 of the Michigan Wolverines reacts after a first half tackle against the Western Michigan Broncos at Michigan Stadium on September 05, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images)

Nobody who watched Michigan, outside fans of the program, thinks they escaped Western Michigan with a last-second win. They were outplayed, couldn't get the Broncos offense off the field, frequently benefited from questionable officiating, then required a miraculous Hail Mary, that should never have happened, to escape with the win. Even including that 47-yard pass, the Wolverines had just 276 yards of offense. At home. Against Western Michigan as a 28-point favorite.

CLOCK CONTROVERSY ALLOWS MICHIGAN WOLVERINES TO AVOID MASSIVE UPSET AGAINST WESTERN MICHIGAN

They averaged 5.8 yards per play, again, with that 47-yard pass included. Bryce Underwood, making an enormous amount of money after a high-profile recruiting war, looked awful. Excluding the Hail Mary, Underwood had 11 completions on 21 pass attempts for 123 yards. Against Western Michigan, at home. The Michigan running game, long a point of pride in Ann Arbor, had 16 attempts from its running backs, for 59 yards. At home. Against Western Michigan. Broncos running back Jalen Buckley had 19 carries for 62 yards. By himself.

A sloppy early season performance isn't enough to fully end a team's season, just ask Notre Dame in 2024, who lost 16-14 to Northern Illinois, then played in the College Football Playoff National Championship game. But with most observers treating Michigan's performance as a loss, and a tough schedule with Oklahoma next weekend, games against Iowa, Penn State, Indiana, Oregon, and Ohio State, it's hard to see the Wolverines as a realistic contender for a playoff spot.

USC though? Their defense finally put in the type of performance fans have been waiting for.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Fresno State isn't Oregon, of course, but the Bulldogs were expected to be one of the better Group of Six teams. They finished 2025 at 9-4, beat Boise State 30-7 and Oregon State 36-27. Many believed they could compete near the top of the newly reconfigured Pac-12 Conference, with analyst Greg McIlroy picking them as the G6 playoff representative.

OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

But the Trojans ran them off the field. SC were 21-point favorites, then outgained the Bulldogs 552-116. They averaged 8.1 yards per play, while allowing just 2.6. Most of Fresno's offensive stats came from the last drive of the game against the SC backups. Midway through the fourth quarter, the Trojans defense had allowed just over 50 total yards on offense and 1.7 yards per play. Fresno State isn't an FCS team. They were No. 73 in preseason SP+, one of the best analytics-driven ranking systems available. That's ahead of teams like Stanford and USF, and not far off from Colorado and Iowa State.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

USC has a tough road ahead too, with games against Oregon, Washington, Ohio State, Indiana, and Penn State ahead, but if the Trojans defense is for real, they might suddenly be, finally, "back."

LSU HAD A REVIVAL, CLEMSON WAS AT A FUNERAL: LANE KIFFIN’S DEBUT SENDS A LOUD MESSAGE TO COLLEGE FOOTBALL

LSU Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt scrambles against Clemson Tigers during the second half at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, La., on Sept. 5, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

No question though, the most impressive of the weekend had to be the LSU Tigers. Despite the controversy surrounding the program, Lane Kiffin's debut couldn't have been better. LSU obliterated Clemson, who were hopeless offensively, and barely able to provide opposition defensively. The Tigers treated the other Tigers like an FCS team, and immediately cemented themselves as top contenders in the SEC, along with Texas and Georgia.

Nothing's decided in week one, but we did, already, see the playoff picture get a shakeup. LSU and USC might be better than expected, with both providing more competition for Ohio State and Georgia than many believed heading into the season.

Oregon, while they clearly "deserved" the win, seem a bit further away from championship quality than many projected based on the talent Dan Lanning's accumulated. And Michigan, well, if poll voters were honest about what everyone saw, they deserve to fall out of the top-25 entirely.

articles.title: Amazon cargo plane crashes in US while landing at Miami airport
articles.excerpt: A cargo plane for the retail company Amazon has crashed in the United States after overrunning its runway while landing at Miami International Airport, disrupting one of the country’s busiest airports...
articles.body_text:
A cargo plane for the retail company Amazon has crashed in the United States after overrunning its runway while landing at Miami International Airport, disrupting one of the country’s busiest airports.

In a post on social media, the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said a Boeing 767-300 aircraft overran the runway at 2pm ET (6pm GMT) upon arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico.

Miami-Dade Fire Rescue said “multiple vehicles” were struck by the plane, which caught on fire after it crashed. The department said it was working to extinguish the blaze and is assessing the status of people affected by the crash.

It’s not clear how many crew members or passengers were on board the plane. No details regarding potential injuries or fatalities were provided.

An Amazon spokesperson said the plane was operated by 21 Air and experienced “an incident” while attempting to land.

“We’re working closely with local authorities and officials to understand exactly what happened,” Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel said. “Right now, our absolute priority is the safety, wellbeing, and care of everyone involved. We’re doing everything we can to support those affected.”

Videos circulating online show black smoke billowing from the scene near the runway. Early reports indicated that the aircraft veered off the runway and crossed a road near the airport.

The US National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), which investigates major transportation-related accidents, confirmed that it was aware of the crash and would provide additional updates as more information became available.

US Department of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said his agency had issued a full ground stop in Miami after the incident, urging travellers to anticipate “significant delays”.

The cause of the incident is unknown. The FAA said it is investigating.

articles.title: At least 10 killed in central Mexico fireworks blast during festival
articles.excerpt:
At least 10 people have been killed and at least 60 wounded in Mexico when fireworks detonated during a village festival, according to the local government.

Video showed revellers carrying a bull mad...
articles.body_text:
At least 10 people have been killed and at least 60 wounded in Mexico when fireworks detonated during a village festival, according to the local government.

Video showed revellers carrying a bull made of straw, with fireworks spouting out of the effigy in Santa Maria Canchesda in the Temascalcingo municipality in central Mexico. The AFP news agency reported that the celebration on Saturday was part of a local ritual.

The burning bull apparently ignited a larger store of fireworks in the village church. The explosion knocked down walls and ignited a fire in the town square, according to the news agency.

Local media reported that some people were trapped under falling debris from the blast.

The diocese of the nearby municipality of Atlacomulco said two priests were injured but are expected to survive.

“We join together in prayer for those who have lost their lives, their families and loved ones, as well as those who were injured and all those who are experiencing moments of pain and worry today,” the diocese said in a statement on social media.

Mexico’s Attorney General’s Office said the cause of the explosion has not been determined and an investigation has opened.

Firework mishaps have previously been deadly in Mexico. In July 2018, an explosion killed 24 people at a fireworks factory in the city of Tultepec, north of Mexico City.

Two years earlier, 42 people died in another fireworks explosion in a market in the city.

articles.title: Hasan Piker brushes off Dems who see him as a liability, names his '28 choice
articles.excerpt:
Far-left influencer Hasan Piker explains why Democrats should study the boldness of President Donald Trump and the MAGA movement.

Hasan Piker hears the growing chorus of Democrats condemning him for ...
articles.body_text:
Far-left influencer Hasan Piker explains why Democrats should study the boldness of President Donald Trump and the MAGA movement.

Hasan Piker hears the growing chorus of Democrats condemning him for incendiary statements, and he has a message for the party: "My job is not to make the Democratic Party look good."

The far-left Twitch streamer has boosted socialist candidates even as he created headaches for the broader Democratic Party in a midterm election cycle where it hopes to make major gains. The 35-year-old Piker — whose polarizing stances range from defending communist Chinese dictator Mao Zedong to comparing Zionism to "Nazism" — is a darling of the Democratic Socialists of America, but a potential liability for mainstream Democrats as November approaches.

Piker said Democratic Party officials have not reached out to coordinate a strategy.

"I have not had a conversation with anyone from the DNC," Piker said. "That would be very funny."

JAMES CARVILLE DECRIES 'IDIOT' HASAN PIKER, ORDERS DSA TO CHANGE ITS NAME

In an exclusive interview at the 2026 Socialism Conference in Chicago, Piker told Fox News that, while he tries "to be as careful as possible" when it comes to choosing his words, his hours-long streams present his opponents with the "perfect opportunity to create viral media moments."

Twitch streamer Hasan Piker appeared on the campaign trail with Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

Some of those moments include intense backlash over Piker’s 2019 statement that America "deserved 9/11," a comment which has been widely condemned by politicians on both sides of the aisle.

HASAN PIKER CALLS REPUBLICAN PARTY THE 'BIGGEST DOMESTIC TERRORIST' IN THE COUNTRY

Piker acknowledged that he should not have used the word "deserved," but said his point was that "[America’s] meddling in the affairs in the Middle East actually transpired these horrifying events."

"It's not a controversial thing [to argue]," Piker said. "It was the language that I used that was controversial."

HASAN PIKER CALLS HAMAS 'FAR MORE MODERATE,' DISMISSES TERROR GROUP’S BRUTAL RULE IN GAZA

Piker's brash commentary gives him credence with the far-left DSA, which pulled off a host of primary victories against more moderate Democrats, but party elders have disavowed him.

Democratic strategist James Carville sharply criticized far-left Democrats for targeting longtime incumbents in primary elections in a video posted Friday for Politicon. (Politicon/YouTube)

"There’s two things that I know about Hasan Piker," longtime Democratic Party consultant James Carville told Fox News Channel last week. "One, he’s an idiot, and two, he’s not a Democrat. So, I don’t answer for idiots, and I don’t answer for people who are not Democrats."

VAN JONES WARNS FAR-LEFT SOCIALIST AGENDA IS 'REGRESSIVE' THREAT TO DEMOCRATIC PARTY

Key Democrat lawmakers, including House Minority Leader Hakeen Jeffries, senators Cory Booker, D-N.J., and Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., and several House members have condemned Piker's past rhetoric.

As he crosses the country, joining campaign rallies and canvass launches for liberal challengers to establishment-backed candidates, Piker acknowledged that even his allies have urged him to moderate his rhetoric for the sake of their electoral chances.

DEMOCRATS' CIVIL WAR HEADS TO MICHIGAN WHERE PROGRESSIVES FACE BIGGEST TEST YET IN HIGH-STAKES SENATE SHOWDOWN

But Piker told Fox News the press is overstating his association with the progressive political candidates and wondered why the media had not "demanded condemnations from establishment Republicans for collaborating with Charlie Kirk or using him as a campaign surrogate."

Piker campaigned hard for Abdul El-Sayed, the progressive Michigan Democratic Senate nominee who pulled off a major upset victory against the establishment-backed Rep. Haley Stevens, D- Mich., in August. While his active support for El-Sayed may have generated buzz among Piker's base, it's also led El-Sayed to face a barrage of questions and criticism about his association with Piker.

GRETCHEN WHITMER ENDORSES MODERATE HALEY STEVENS IN TIGHT UPCOMING SENATE PRIMARY

Piker said that while he is confident El-Sayed – who distanced himself from Piker in recent weeks – will win this fall, "if people want to blame me" in the event El-Sayed loses, "they can blame me," adding, "I think that's the goal."

Hasan Piker named Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez as his preferred presidential candidate over a slate of high-profile Democrats. (Getty Images)

Piker's role in the midterms may prove to be a warmup for the 2028 presidential election, and he said he has no plans to moderate his stances or stay on the sidelines. He said he will back socialist Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y. if she launches a bid for the Democratic Party's presidential nomination.

WATCH: AOC WON'T RULE OUT WHITE HOUSE BID AFTER POLL NAMES HER DEMOCRATS' TOP 2028 PICK

"I think she's great," Piker said. "She would have some difficulties, of course, but hurdles can be climbed over, and I think she can do it."

Piker believes his influence will continue to grow, and predicted even Democrats now condemning him will "try to utilize the platform that I have" if they seek higher office in 2028.

2028 BATTLEGROUND POLL SCRAMBLES DEMOCRATS’ FUTURE AS INSURGENT SOCIALIST SEIZES LEAD

"And I'm not talking about my ideological allies or people who are associated with me right now," he added.

Matthew Donnell is a Campaign Embed at FOX News and an Assignment Editor at FOX Business.

articles.body_text:

A deadly argument outside a Nashville lounge sent a bullet tearing through the metal wall of a nearby Sam’s Club, killing an innocent Frito-Lay worker as he counted products in the chip aisle, police said.

The victim, identified as 55-year-old Paris Carlock of Murfreesboro, was conducting an early-morning product inventory near the middle of the store shortly after 4 a.m. when the bullet struck him in the head.

Sam’s Club staff rushed to Carlock’s aid before he was transported to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead, according to the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department.

POLICE SEARCH FOR GUNMAN AFTER WALMART EMPLOYEE SHOT DURING DISPUTE IN PENNSYLVANIA

A Metro Nashville Police vehicle sits outside the Sam’s Club where Frito-Lay employee Paris Carlock was fatally struck by a bullet that pierced the store’s wall. (Metropolitan Nashville Police Department)

Investigators believe the gunfire was connected to an argument that began inside Lavo Lounge on Antioch Pike, just down the street from the Sam’s Club.

Police said security removed the people involved from the lounge, but the dispute reportedly spilled outside and continued. Gunshots were heard as multiple vehicles left the area.

MISSOURI MOM OF 5 FATALLY SHOT WHILE BUYING SLUSHIES WITH CHILDREN; POLICE SEARCH FOR GUNMAN

A bullet from gunfire on Antioch Pike pierced the metal side wall of a Sam’s Club and struck Paris Carlock as he conducted inventory inside, police said. (Metropolitan Nashville Police Department)

One of those bullets pierced the Sam’s Club’s exterior wall and struck Carlock as he worked inside, police said.

The department described Carlock as an "innocent" victim.

POLICE SWARM MICHIGAN SHOPPING CENTER AFTER 'SIGNIFICANT' SHOOTING INCIDENT; AT LEAST 2 DEAD

Police said an argument began inside Lavo Lounge before spilling outside and ending in gunfire that killed an innocent Frito-Lay worker inside a nearby Sam’s Club. (Google Maps)

Homicide Unit detectives are pursuing leads, but police have not announced any arrests or released descriptions of the people or vehicles involved.

Anyone with information about the gunfire or the vehicles seen leaving the area is asked to call Nashville Crime Stoppers at 615-742-7463.

Fox News Digital reached out to Frito-Lay for comment.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

articles.title: Cody Rhodes says 'that addiction and sickness' to win WWE title again is more on Randy Orton's end
articles.excerpt:
WWE star Cody Rhodes responds to Randy Orton's SmackDown promo in an interview with OutKick before Sunday Night's Main Event.

Cody Rhodes’ relationship with Randy Orton has been fraught with tension ...
articles.body_text:
WWE star Cody Rhodes responds to Randy Orton's SmackDown promo in an interview with OutKick before Sunday Night's Main Event.

Cody Rhodes’ relationship with Randy Orton has been fraught with tension since the "Legend Killer" returned to "Friday Night SmackDown" to reignite his feud with the "American Nightmare."

The two had come to blows numerous times before SmackDown GM Nick Aldis said the two couldn’t lay a finger on each other before their match at Sunday Night’s Main Event in Atlanta and if they did, they would have been barred from competing for a WWE championship.

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK

Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton speak during SmackDown at Canadian Tire Centre in Ottawa, Ontario, on Aug. 28, 2026. (WWE via Getty Images)

In their last face-to-face meeting, Orton tried to coax Rhodes into hitting him with strong words about how Rhodes was an "addict" and "sick" for his desire to be the champion. But when it comes to pro wrestling, why was that a bad thing?

Rhodes responded to Orton’s words in an interview with OutKick Dropkick.

"He had said, ‘addicted to winning the championship’ and ‘sick’ and putting it in front of everything. What's the term kids use today? The rage bait, you know, or baiting me into ... because if I had hit him, then I don't get an opportunity for the WWE championship ever, and the same vice versa if he had hit me," Rhodes said. "I hate to put it in such terms, but at King of the Ring, I beat Randy Orton. At WrestleMania, I beat Randy Orton. I feel the desperation and the addiction. Every pro wrestler, to your point, you're in this to win. You're not trying to get second on the podium. I've never trusted a wrestler ever — hell, I've never liked a wrestler ever — who said he didn't want to be champion.

Cody Rhodes looks on during SummerSlam at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, Minn., on Aug. 1, 2026. (WWE via Getty Images)

"But I think that addiction and sickness is actually more on Randy's end because Randy's close to the record. He's close to 17. He's close to John. I think Randy also feels that he's not been given the credit as one of the, you know, the GOATs of modern WWE, someone who's going to go down in history as one of the greatest to ever do it. He should know he is going to go down in history as one of the greatest to ever do it, but he's also going to go down in history as the guy who lost for a third time at Sunday Night's Main Event to his protege, which is me."

Rhodes, who spoke to OutKick Dropkick as part of his partnership with Clash of Clans and its new "Search for Cena" event, is among those vying to get back into the Undisputed WWE Championship picture.

This match between Rhodes and Orton will certainly clear the picture up a little bit as Money in the Bank inches closer.

Randy Orton faces Cody Rhodes during WrestleMania 42: Night 1 at Allegiant Stadium on April 18, 2026, in Las Vegas, Nev. (WWE via Getty Images)

Sunday Night’s Main Event will also feature a six-woman tag team match between the team of Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley and the team of Jade Cargill, Michin and B-Fab, a match between Baron Corbin and Lil Yachty and a bout between Oba Femi and Bron Breakker.

Ryan Gaydos is a senior editor for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Peace talks rich in symbolism but fundamental differences between Russia and Ukraine remain
articles.excerpt:
The talks in Kyiv were rich in symbolism. The sight of Donald Trump's envoys setting foot on Ukrainian soil for the first time since Russia's full-scale invasion.

The fact they had to travel by train...
articles.body_text:
The talks in Kyiv were rich in symbolism. The sight of Donald Trump's envoys setting foot on Ukrainian soil for the first time since Russia's full-scale invasion.

The fact they had to travel by train because they could not risk flying and running the gauntlet of Russian drones - weapons launched on the orders of the man at whose table they sat in the Kremlin only hours ago.

The symbolism of Ukrainian President Zelensky greeting Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner at Kyiv's Saint Sophia Cathedral, not only an icon of Ukraine's ancient history, but also just a few yards from where Russian drones hit the headquarters of the country's security services on Friday.

You did not have to join too many dots to work out the point Zelensky was making.

Both sides held talks for several hours; they were later joined by some European national security advisers, including the UK's National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell.

And afterwards, all sides spoke warmly of having held substantive discussions. They spoke hopefully of reviving past "trilateral talks" involving both the US and Europe.

But fundamental differences remain. The US envoys had come hot foot from Moscow where Vladimir Putin had told them Russia was making "tangible advances" on the battlefield.

The story they heard from Ukraine was different, in fact the opposite. Ukrainian officials claim that in August they gained more territory than they lost and Russia suffered 42,000 casualties, dead or wounded.

Putin had also told the US envoys the root causes of the conflict had to be addressed, shorthand for his longstanding strategic demands that Ukraine cede territory, abandon hopes of joining Nato and reduce the size of its army.

After the talks, Zelensky insisted Ukraine would require "strong and clear" security guarantees, including a strong army. Nor did he give any sign of being willing to give up any territory in the eastern Donbas region, an issue he described dryly as "difficult".

Watch: President Zelensky welcomes US envoys in Kyiv

Witkoff insisted progress had been made and the ingredients for a settlement were there.

But he admitted both sides would have to make compromises to narrow the differences between them. And right now, it is hard to see either side doing that.

So for now, the expectation in Kyiv is that the fighting will continue and they will face a hard winter ahead.

Some diplomats talk of a window of opportunity for a possible settlement next spring. Others are less optimistic.

Zelensky thanked the US envoys for their visit because the short-term pause in air strikes agreed by both sides had given the people of Kyiv a brief respite. Few expect it to last for long.

articles.title: How a booming coastal escape learned to coexist with the ocean’s top predator
articles.excerpt:
Wildlife biologist Forrest Galante shares tips for avoiding sharks in the ocean this summer on 'The Will Cain Show.'

As great white sharks increasingly frequent the waters off one popular seaside des...
articles.body_text:
Wildlife biologist Forrest Galante shares tips for avoiding sharks in the ocean this summer on 'The Will Cain Show.'

As great white sharks increasingly frequent the waters off one popular seaside destination, tourists are flocking there, too — but they’re experiencing the hot spot in a different way.

Cape Cod is a renowned seaside destination in southeastern Massachusetts that has long drawn summer vacationers with its picturesque beaches, historic coastal towns and lighthouses. In recent years, though, it has also become increasingly known for its seasonal population of great white sharks.

Far from deterring visitors, the presence of sharks is helping fuel a whole new type of tourism.

SHARK WEEK ADVISORY AS WARMING SEAS PUSH BLACKTIPS FARTHER NORTH ALONG EAST COAST

The New York Times reported that Cape Cod’s tourism economy has grown from nearly $2 billion in 2019 to almost $2.8 billion, according to the Cape Cod Chamber of Commerce.

At the same time, the National Park Service has recorded fewer recreational visits to Cape Cod National Seashore, the 40-mile stretch of coastline where white sharks are regularly detected.

Shark warning signs and "Stop the Bleed" rescue kits are now fixtures on the beaches.

Cape Cod has long attracted summer vacationers with its picturesque beaches, historic coastal towns and lighthouses. (Joseph Prezioso / AFP) (Photo by JOSEPH PREZIOSO/AFP via Getty Images)

The Atlantic White Shark Conservancy created and runs Sharktivity, a shark-sighting and resource app designed to keep beachgoers apprised of the sharks’ presence. It features alerts for confirmed white shark sightings close to public beaches, along with other shark-safety information.

The increased presence of great white sharks in Cape Cod’s waters has been linked to the recovery of the Cape’s gray seal population following the passage of the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972. The seal population grew from around 2,000 in 1994 to between 30,000 and 50,000 in 2017, the Times reported.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

A 2023 study published in the peer-reviewed journal Marine Ecology Progress Series estimated that roughly 800 individual white sharks visited the waters off Cape Cod between 2015 and 2018, making the area one of the world’s larger white shark hot spots.

Despite their growing presence, there is no evidence Cape Cod’s white sharks have become more aggressive or changed their behavior by hunting closer to shore, according to the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy. The sharks have hunted seals in shallow coastal waters since they began predictably returning to the area during the summer and fall.

"Sharks have changed behaviors and conversations more than they’ve changed demand," Paul Bordé, a local real estate agent, told the Times.

Hundreds of individual great white sharks visit the waters off Cape Cod, making the area a major seasonal hot spot for the predators. (iStock)

When life gives your town sharks, make shark-spotting profitable.

Cape Cod is a rising "white shark ecotourism destination," according to the Times. Shark seekers can hire a private charter through the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy for $2,500 or join an open-boat charter for $500 per person.

The 2½-hour trips use spotter pilots to locate sharks, and private charters can book up weeks or even a month in advance, according to the conservancy.

The excursions aren’t purely sightseeing trips. Guests can participate in citizen science by logging shark sightings, using a hydrophone to detect tagged sharks and recording observations that contribute to ongoing research.

Because the trips directly support white shark research, a portion of the trip fee is tax-deductible, the conservancy writes on its website.

Beachgoers share Cape Cod’s coastal waters with great white sharks, which return to the area seasonally to hunt seals. (John Tlumacki/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)

"The fact that we can go out and see them in a two-and-a-half-hour charter is incredibly unique," Hannah Leary, ecotourism coordinator for the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy, told the Times. "We can just come out of the inlet and they’re all right there."

The shark presence may also be benefiting some swimming pool companies. Demand for pools has "spiked," the Times reported, and "one Cape Cod pool builder even advertises ‘shark free swimming’ on its trucks."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The great white sharks’ presence has not been all adventurous sightseeing and tourism dollars, however.

A bodysurfer was bitten by a white shark in the area in 2012, and a swimmer was bitten in 2018. Both survived, but later in 2018, Massachusetts recorded its first fatal shark attack since 1936 when a white shark killed a 26-year-old boogie boarder.

Purple shark flags at Cape Cod National Seashore beaches alert visitors that a shark sighting has occurred. (Joseph Prezioso/AFP via Getty Images)

"I understand the fear," Philadelphia resident Lisa DonDiego told the Times. "And at the end of the day, I recognize that the ocean belongs to them. But I still want to come to Cape Cod."

The National Park Service urges beachgoers to stay away from seals and schools of fish, swim in groups and avoid murky or low-visibility water. Purple shark flags at National Seashore beaches indicate that there has been a shark sighting, and swimmers are urged to follow all posted warnings and lifeguard instructions.

White shark activity also extends beyond Cape Cod’s peak summer season. The National Park Service warns that the predators remain active in the fall, even after seasonal lifeguard coverage ends at National Seashore beaches.

Teresa Mull is a freelance writer with the Lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Amazon cargo plane crashes at Miami airport and hits several vehicles
articles.excerpt:
FAA confirms crash and airport operations brought to a halt as videos show heavy plumes of smoke surrounding aircraft

An Amazon cargo plane crashed at Miami international airport in Florida on Sunday...
articles.body_text:
FAA confirms crash and airport operations brought to a halt as videos show heavy plumes of smoke surrounding aircraft

An Amazon cargo plane crashed at Miami international airport in Florida on Sunday afternoon after the flight, which was arriving from Puerto Rico, overshot the runway, striking several vehicles and erupting in flames as dark smoke billowed into the sky, bringing operations at one of the busiest airports in the US to a halt.

Videos posted online show heavy plumes of smoke surrounding an aircraft bearing the Amazon arrow logo on its tail. Unconfirmed reports suggest there may be casualties, but details about injuries or fatalities remained unclear.

The plane was a Boeing 767 flying for Amazon Prime Air.

The Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) confirmed the crash in a statement to the Guardian, saying: “21 Air Flight 7598 overran the runway after landing at Miami International Airport around 2 pm local time on Sunday, September 6. The Boeing 767-300 cargo aircraft departed from Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The FAA will investigate.”

The plane overran the airport’s diagonal runway and was disabled at the north-west end of the airport, a spokesperson for Miami international airport said.

An air and ground stop has been issued at the airport, preventing all other flights from landing or taking off at the busy south Florida hub.

“All runways and taxiways at MIA are currently closed as of 3pm and a ground stop is in effect,” the airport said, adding: “Miami-Dade Fire Rescue has responded to the scene.”

More than 60 units from the Miami-Dade fire rescue services appeared on scene, with units arriving “to find an airplane that had caught on fire as a result of this crash, with heavy flames and smoke showing”, the fire department said, with the post adding that the plane had struck multiple vehicles near the airport.

Firefighters were “working on extinguishing the fire and assessing patients”, the post on Twitter/X said.

US transportation secretary Sean Duffy said on X that responders would “assess the scene after an Amazon cargo plane overran the runway”.

“If you’re traveling through the area, please expect significant delays and potential cancellations,” he added.

Meanwhile, the Miami-Dade sheriff’s office announced street closures due to the crash, saying on X: “NW 67th Avenue between NW 25th Street – NW 36th Street is currently closed. Expect delays and seek alternate routes.”

Kelly Nantel, an Amazon spokesperson told the Guardian in a statement: “We can confirm that an Amazon Air plane operated by 21 Air experienced an incident while attempting to land at Miami International Airport today. This is a fast-moving situation and we’re still gathering details.

“We’re working closely with local authorities and officials to understand exactly what happened. Right now, our absolute priority is the safety, well-being, and care of everyone involved. We’re doing everything we can to support those affected.”

The Guardian has reached out to the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) for comment.

articles.title: Fisherman captures a crazy video of an alligator chasing a bear across a Florida river

articles.body_text:
NASCAR star Chase Elliott reflects on spending part of his childhood in Colorado and explains how hiking, snowboarding and mountain life helped shape his love of nature during an interview with OutKick Outdoors.

Let's head down to Florida where anything can and does take place. If you can dream it up, there's a good chance it will go down in the Sunshine State. That goes for both people and animals.

The latest example to prove that point comes from a fisherman out on the Kissimmee river near Lake Okeechobee. Captain Justin Morgan, who runs a fishing guide service, captured the crazy video.

Stock image of bear and alligator. (Getty Images/iStockphoto)

The clip shows a scene that you don't see every day, a bear swimming across the river with an alligator hot on its trail chasing it towards the shore.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

"Alligator tracking down a bear across the Kissimmee river near Lake Okeechobee," the captain captioned the action.

"We were out bluegill fishing when what from a distance looked like a wild hog was a black bear swimming across the Kissimmee with a gator not far behind! Not something we get to see everyday but really cool to watch!"

SON OF FLORIDA ALLIGATOR ATTACK VICTIM SAYS TOURISTS AND TIKTOKERS ARE EMBOLDENING THE GATORS

This was close to giving us a straight out of a nature documentary look at what would happen if an alligator and a black bear ever went at it in the wild.

That begs the question. What would happen? Did the alligator give chase after mistaking the bear for something else it could easily take down?

Stock image of a bear swimming. (Getty Images)

Does the advantage lean towards the alligator in the water and the bear on land? That's what I would assume.

GEAR UP FOR FALL WITH LABOR DAY DEALS ON HUNTING, FISHING, CAMPING AND OUTDOOR LIVING ESSENTIALS

A bear did successfully fend off a couple of alligators trying to attack it in the water before, but is that how they always play out or do alligators put some in the win column?

Stock image of an alligator eating another alligator. (Getty Images/iStockphoto)

In this case, the alligator appears to lose interest once the bear makes it to the shore. The bear takes a look back before wandering into the woods and doesn’t seem interested in the alligator either.

articles.title: Hawaii declares state of emergency as Hurricane Lowell approaches islands
articles.excerpt:
Storm, which may make impact as soon as Monday, is third system in weeks to threaten state during hurricane season

Hawaii has declared a state of emergency as powerful Hurricane Lowell makes its way ...
articles.body_text:
Storm, which may make impact as soon as Monday, is third system in weeks to threaten state during hurricane season

Hawaii has declared a state of emergency as powerful Hurricane Lowell makes its way toward the islands, with the first impacts expected as soon as Monday.

The storm is the third system in just over three weeks to threaten Hawaii during an active hurricane season in the central Pacific. Lowell remained a category 3 hurricane early on Sunday morning, packing winds of 125 miles per hour while moving north-west at six miles per hour.

According to the forecast, Lowell will reach Hawaii as a category 2 hurricane. Its center could pass roughly 130 miles west of Ni’ihau or 170 miles west of Kauai between Monday evening and Tuesday morning.

The threat comes amid unusually intense hurricane activity across the Pacific.

As of Saturday, Hurricanes Karina, Lowell and Marie were all churning in the Pacific at the same time, marking the region’s first triple-hurricane stretch in a decade. The National Hurricane Center (NHC) was also monitoring a fourth potential system off the coast of Mexico.

The Pacific averages only eight hurricanes per year, according to the NHC, making three simultaneous hurricanes highly unusual.

Lowell’s projected offshore path is expected to keep the storm’s most dangerous winds away from Hawaii’s islands. But heavy rain, high surf and dangerous coastal conditions are still expected.

A tropical storm warning is in effect for Kauai and Ni’ihau, where wind gusts above 39 miles per hour are possible over the next 48 hours.

Lowell is the third storm in a matter of weeks to hit Hawaii as the climate crisis continues to increase the intensity and frequency of storms and other weather events.

Tropical Storm Moke struck the southern part of Hawaii’s islands two weeks ago, bringing heavy rainfall and strong winds. That came just days after Hurricane Lala hit the region.

The Hawaii governor Josh Green said Lala alone had caused at least $43m in infrastructure damage on the Big Island, along with another $4.6m in damage to homes.

The escalating storm activity comes as the UN warns that this year’s El Niño is forecast to become the strongest on record in four decades.

A statement released on Thursday described El Niño as being “supersized before our eyes”, adding that the world is in “the danger zone of extreme weather”.

The latest data on the natural climate phenomenon shows a near 100% likelihood that the latest El Niño will continue through February 2027, the statement said. The stronger an El Niño becomes, the greater the chance it will significantly alter rainfall and temperature patterns around the world and help fuel extreme weather.

The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) has previously warned there is a 69% chance that this El Niño will be the strongest in 70 years.

articles.title: Woman laid to rest in coffin made from mushrooms in Australian first
articles.excerpt:
The casket, grown from mycelium and hemp fibres, takes just 45 days to break down, enriching the soil in the process

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A woman has been buri...
articles.body_text:
The casket, grown from mycelium and hemp fibres, takes just 45 days to break down, enriching the soil in the process

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A woman has been buried in a coffin made from mushrooms in New South Wales in an eco-friendly first for Australia.

Carolyn, aged in her 70s, was laid to rest on Friday by friends and family at Springwood Cemetery in the Blue Mountains.

The mushroom coffin, created by the Dutch firm Loop Biotech, was grown from mycelium – the root network of fungi – and hemp fibres.

The coffin is grown in mould in a climate-controlled room, taking just a week to fully form. Once buried, it takes about 45 days to become part of the soil.

The process is akin to composting, as the body and coffin gently biodegrade and transform into nutrient-rich soil in far less time than a traditional wooden casket, which can take up to 50 years to break down.

Carolyn’s husband, David, said picking the mushroom coffin aligned with his wife’s values of giving back.

“She was always there to help others. It feels very true to who she was that even after her death, she can still do something for others while giving something back to nature,” he said.

While Carolyn is the first to be buried in the coffin in Australia, Loop Biotech’s founder Bob Hendrikx said there had been thousands of others across Europe and the US.

“Five years ago when I started, there was lots of interest from Australia,” Hendrikx said. “It was a little bit harder to ship overseas [at the time].”

Hendrikx hopes the mushroom coffins, which weigh about 30kg each, could improve the sustainability of the Australian funeral sector by shortening the decomposition process.

“It’s about giving back to nature: we have the mushroom, which is grown and dissolves into nature, but the actual benefit is that … it’s enriching the soil,” he said.

“The body needs to just return to nature and let nature do what it’s done best forever.

“If a kangaroo dies in the forest, it’s just going to be part of the cycle of life.”

Dr Hannah Gould, a cultural anthropologist at the University of Melbourne, believes people are becoming increasingly interested in environmentally friendly farewells.

“As people perhaps become less religious, other kinds of values or community groupings become more important, and one of those that we’ve seen is eco-death.

“This idea that perhaps that you don’t go up to heaven after you die, you return to the earth, has been an increasingly popular narrative around death and dying.”

While about 70% of Australians choose to be cremated, it has a substantial environmental impact: the emissions from a typical cremation are estimated to be equivalent to 125kg of carbon dioxide.

In recent years options such as alkaline hydrolysis (a cremation-like process that uses water instead of fire), natural burials without embalming, and even shallow burials have become available. A natural burial uses a cardboard coffin with rope handles and will emit less than 10kg of carbon dioxide equivalent, according to PlanetMark analysis.

Gould believes that as Australians are living longer and more people are dying from prolonged illnesses, more time is being spent thinking about how to depart and farewell loved ones.

“They’ve maybe seen or organised a funeral for their parents and it hasn’t gone so well,” she said. “And they’re now deciding that they want to do things differently. So we’re seeing a huge rise in funeral planning.”

articles.title: Adidas faces boycott calls over campaign featuring former Israeli soldier
articles.excerpt:
Adidas faces boycott calls over campaign featuring former Israeli soldier

Sportswear giant Adidas has faced criticism and calls for a boycott for featuring a former Israeli army soldier in an adverti...
articles.body_text:
Adidas faces boycott calls over campaign featuring former Israeli soldier

Sportswear giant Adidas has faced criticism and calls for a boycott for featuring a former Israeli army soldier in an advertising campaign for the company’s single-shoe service for amputees.

The Adidas advertisement promoting its in-store service, which shows former Israeli soldier Shalev Biton trying on a shoe at a store in Israel and then wearing it while running outdoors, was termed “an affront to Palestinians” by a boycott campaigns coordinator on Sunday.

Biton lost his leg after being wounded during the 2021 Israel-Gaza conflict, during which the Israeli army attacked the besieged enclave repeatedly in an 11-day assault.

Human rights campaigners and pro-Palestine activists say the immediate outrage and online boycott campaign targeted at Adidas should not come as a surprise to the German athletic apparel and footwear company.

“This isn’t Adidas being tone-deaf or insensitive; it is an absolute affront to the Palestinians who have lost their loved ones, killed by Israel, and who have lost their limbs [to Israeli attacks],” Stephanie Westbrook, a sports boycott campaigns coordinator for the Palestinian Campaign for the Academic and Cultural Boycott of Israel (PACBI) – a founding member of the Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions (BDS) movement – told Al Jazeera.

Westbrook underlined the danger of such campaigns, which she believes would “normalise Israel’s crimes against Palestinians and allow it to continue to commit them with impunity”.

“Here we have an Adidas campaign featuring an Israeli soldier, whose whole identity is centred around his being a soldier, who lost his leg while participating in one of the repeated Israeli assaults on Gaza, serving in an army of a state that is currently committing genocide, has carried out an illegal military occupation of the Palestinian territory, and that has been imposing a decades-long apartheid rule over Palestinians,” she said.

The World Health Organization estimates that between 5,000 and 6,000 people in Gaza have undergone amputations as of early October 2025, when Israel and Hamas signed a “ceasefire” agreement. They are among the 42,000 Palestinians in Gaza who have sustained life-changing injuries during the two-year conflict.

Nearly a year since the ceasefire, conditions remain dire due to Israel’s blockage of humanitarian aid from entering the enclave.

While the advertisement shows the soldier returning to the streets to exercise and run, more than one thousand Palestinian athletes have been killed during Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

Hundreds of aspiring footballers have lost their limbs and have formed amputee football teams, finding some respite in sport despite their pain.

These players hold on to football as a means of survival and are trying to reclaim fragments of their former lives despite months of loss, injuries, and widespread destruction.

Spanish actor Javier Bardem was among those calling for a boycott of the sportswear brand. Bardem, who is a vocal pro-Palestine activist, shared several images and videos highlighting the boycott campaign on his social media accounts.

US-Palestinian author Susan Abulhawa, Pakistani author Fatima Bhutto, and Palestinians on social media called for a boycott of Adidas products.

Rights campaigner Westbrook highlighted Israel’s blockade on Gaza, which prevents medicines and prosthetics from entering the Gaza Strip following Israeli destruction of the territory’s medical facilities.

Children account for a quarter of all amputations in Gaza over the past two years, making it the place in the world with the highest number of child amputees per capita, according to the International Rescue Committee.

Westbrook said Israel had “decimated the health sector”, causing a severe lack of care and rehabilitation services.

“Its medieval siege is preventing prosthetics from even entering Gaza, creating this man-made shortage,” she added.

Since the Israeli war on Gaza began in October 2023, reports the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), 42,000 Palestinians have suffered life-altering injuries, of which 11,000 are children.

articles.title: Trump administration appeals again to US Supreme Court over mail-in voting
articles.excerpt:
The administration of United States President Donald Trump has made another appeal to the Supreme Court to allow new restrictions on mail-in voting ahead of the midterms in November.

Two days after a...
articles.body_text:
The administration of United States President Donald Trump has made another appeal to the Supreme Court to allow new restrictions on mail-in voting ahead of the midterms in November.

Two days after a federal judge blocked the US Postal Service (USPS) from enforcing Trump’s executive order, the administration on Sunday escalated the matter to the country’s highest court, asking justices to temporarily allow the agency to track mail-in ballots and decide whether they could be rejected. The ongoing legal battle comes even as some states have already begun sending out postal ballots.

US District Judge Indira Talwani issued an order on Friday that said Trump’s directives, which would grant the federal government power over the handling of mail-in ballots, are likely unconstitutional. In the US, elections – including ones for federal office – are carried out by states.

The judge also criticised the timing of the executive order’s implementation, writing that, with just two months until election day, it “threatens disenfranchisement of millions of United States citizens who seek to vote by mail”.

But in its emergency filing on Sunday, the Trump administration countered Talwani’s ruling: “Contrary to the claims of the district court and respondents that the Postal Service is trying to federalise the rules for mail-in voting, the Postal Service’s final rule imposes only modest envelope-design and addressee-information requirements for federal-election ballots sent via U.S. Mail”.

US Solicitor General John Sauer, who argues cases before the Supreme Court on behalf of the federal government, said Trump’s order would not seize control of states’ right to administer elections, but would only impose “reasonable preparation requirements” for mail-in ballots.

“[The rule] requires States to upload the name, address and barcode information of intended recipients of ballot mail in an online portal — information that election officials would necessarily already possess to send ballot mail under the Rule to those recipients,” Sauer wrote in the filing. “The Rule ensures that States remain responsible for determining voter eligibility and eligibility to vote by mail, and it does not dictate ballot content, mailing or receipt deadlines, or ballot-counting procedures.”

Supreme Court Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson set a deadline of Wednesday for responses to the Trump administration’s request.

Sunday’s filing marks the third time the Trump administration has asked the Supreme Court to intervene. The court recently allowed the plan to move forward but did not rule on whether it was legal.

With control of the US Congress up for grabs in November, how the Supreme Court rules on the appeal could have major implications.

Despite voting by mail himself, Trump has long sought to limit it during his time in office, falsely claiming that it is ripe with fraud. Opponents say the president’s motivation is simpler, arguing that Democrats vote by mail more than Republicans.

An analysis conducted by the States United Democracy Center found that many voters, no matter their political affiliation, cast their ballots by mail. The research found that one in four registered Democrats and one in five registered Republicans voted by mail in the 2024 presidential election.

articles.title: Raskin calls Piker’s rhetoric 'irrelevant distraction' after the streamer said he'd vote for Hamas over Israel
articles.excerpt: Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., dismissed scrutiny of Hasan Piker’s rhetoric about Hamas as an "irrelevant distraction" after NBC’s Kristen Welker played a clip of the streamer saying he would "vote for Ham...
articles.body_text:
Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., dismissed scrutiny of Hasan Piker’s rhetoric about Hamas as an "irrelevant distraction" after NBC’s Kristen Welker played a clip of the streamer saying he would "vote for Hamas over Israel every single time."

Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., dismissed scrutiny of far-left streamer Hasan Piker's rhetoric about Hamas as an "irrelevant distraction" Sunday on NBC's "Meet the Press," as host Kristen Welker pressed him over Democratic divisions surrounding Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed's relationship with the controversial online personality.

Welker played Raskin a clip of Piker saying he would vote Hamas over Israel "every single time" and asked whether the Democratic Party’s tent was large enough to include the streamer.

"I don’t even know if Hasan Piker considers himself a Democrat. I know he attacked me for campaigning with Callie Barr and Sean McCann and other Democrats in Michigan. I think all of that is an irrelevant distraction," Raskin said. "Obviously, nobody supports Hamas, a terrorist organization which brutally attacked Israel on October 7th."

Rep. Jamie Raskin dismissed scrutiny of Hasan Piker’s Hamas rhetoric as an "irrelevant distraction" during an appearance on "Meet the Press." (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

STEPHEN A SMITH WARNS HASAN PIKER WILL ‘CONTAMINATE’ DEMOCRATS IN THE MIDTERMS, ‘COME BACK TO HAUNT THEM’

Natalie Baldassarre, national press secretary for the RNC, pointed to Piker’s growing role in Democratic politics and his support for socialist candidates as she warned that his influence could become a broader liability for the party heading into November.

"The Democrat Party is being driven off [a] cliff by socialists who are driving blindfolded while arguing about the view," Baldassarre said in a recent statement to Fox News Digital. "Unless Democrats hit the brakes, every candidate on the ballot will have to answer for socialists’ outrageous beliefs that will bankrupt our country and strip every American of safety, sanity, and freedom."

Raskin's comments came after he campaigned alongside El-Sayed in Michigan in late August. El-Sayed has continued to face questions over his ties to Piker as some Democrats have publicly distanced themselves from the streamer.

Kristen Welker pressed Raskin after playing a clip of Piker saying he would "vote for Hamas over Israel every single time." (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS OF AMERICA BACKS 'OUR TWITCH STREAMER' HASAN PIKER, RIPS ANTI-SOCIALISM HOUSE RESOLUTION

Piker, who endorsed El-Sayed and appeared at multiple campaign events during the Democratic primary, reiterated his comparison between Hamas and Israel during an April appearance on "Pod Save America."

"I’ve also said I’m a harm reduction voter. I’m a lesser evil voter, and therefore I would vote for Hamas over Israel every single time," Piker said in the clip played for Raskin on Sunday.

Piker has also faced renewed criticism for comments involving American Jews. Fox News Digital reported that he warned on a livestream that if American Jews continued presenting themselves as "singularly invested in Israel," someone could eventually "take action" against them.

Piker’s past comments about Hamas and Israel have drawn renewed scrutiny as Democrats face questions over his influence in party politics. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

HASAN PIKER INSISTS ABDUL EL-SAYED ASKED HIM TO 'STUMP' FOR MICHIGAN CAMPAIGN AMID BACKLASH

El-Sayed responded to that controversy by stressing that the streamer was not a spokesman for his campaign.

"I want to be crystal clear, nobody speaks for this campaign besides me and my campaign spokespeople," El-Sayed said.

El-Sayed has nevertheless resisted calls to fully disavow Piker. During a recent interview with Stephen A. Smith, he said his goal was to bring the streamer's millions of listeners into the electoral process rather than abandon them over disagreements.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"What I’m saying is there are three million people who listen to Hasan," El-Sayed said. "I want to offer them a pathway into an electoral movement."

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., called the attention devoted to Piker "absolutely ludicrous," while Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash, said Democrats should engage his audience even if they disagree with some of his views. Other Democrats have urged the party to distance itself from him.

Fox News Digital reached out to Piker for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.
